movies.title: Captain America: The First Avenger
movies.summary: Set during World War II, a frail young man is transformed into a super-soldier and takes on a rogue Nazi-science division bent on world domination, ending with him frozen and lost to time.

beforeWatch.context: The earliest point on the whole timeline, and a clean place to start. It assumes you know nothing. Most of it plays as a 1940s war picture: the Second World War is on, America has just entered it, and the fringe science on both sides is running well ahead of the era. The one thing worth carrying in is that this world's history is our history right up until the point where it isn't.

deepDive.plot: In WWII, scrawny but big-hearted Steve Rogers volunteers for an experimental super-soldier program and becomes Captain America. He spends the rest of the war fighting Hydra's rogue science division, led by the Red Skull, who is chasing a mystical artifact called the Tesseract to power city-destroying weapons. In the climactic battle, Steve crashes an out-of-control plane into the Arctic ice to save the country, and wakes up decades later in the present day, having lost everything and everyone he knew.
deepDive.significance: Sets the standard everyone else gets measured against. Steve is decent before he is strong, and the film is careful to establish that in the first half hour so the rest of the saga can keep referring back to it. It also plants three things that run for a decade: the Tesseract, Hydra, and a man who lost seventy years.
deepDive.orderNote: First because it happens first. The bulk of it runs from 1942 to 1945, decades before anything else here, and it needs nothing in front of it.

watchFor.name: Steve before the serum
watchFor.thisFilm: Five foot four, asthmatic, and lying on enlistment forms in five different cities. Erskine picks him precisely because he has spent his whole life on the receiving end.

watchFor.name: Howard Stark
watchFor.thisFilm: Tony's father, decades younger, building the shield and flying the plane. Worth noticing how competent and how absent he manages to be at the same time.
watchFor.future: Most of what Tony believes about him is shaped by his not being there.

watchFor.name: Bucky Barnes
watchFor.thisFilm: The one person who knew Steve before, and the reason Steve joins the war at all. Falls from a train and everyone writes him off.
watchFor.future: Hydra got to him at the bottom of that ravine, and he spends seventy years as their weapon.

watchFor.name: Peggy Carter
watchFor.thisFilm: An officer who is better at the job than the men around her and stops apologising for it early on. The last conversation is a dance neither of them gets to have.
watchFor.future: Founds S.H.I.E.L.D., and that unfinished dance is the last thing the saga gives Steve.

watchFor.name: The Tesseract
watchFor.thisFilm: Schmidt digs it out of a Norwegian church and builds his war machine on it. Howard Stark fishes it out of the ocean at the end while searching for Steve.
watchFor.future: S.H.I.E.L.D. still has it decades later, which is what Loki comes for.

watchFor.name: Hydra
watchFor.thisFilm: A Nazi science division that outgrows the regime it belongs to. Cut off one head and two more take its place, which the film treats as a boast rather than a warning.
watchFor.future: It was never actually destroyed here.

watchFor.name: What happens to Schmidt
watchFor.thisFilm: Grabs the Tesseract bare-handed and is pulled somewhere by it rather than killed by it.
watchFor.future: It put him on Vormir, keeping watch over the Soul Stone for people who have not been born yet.

watchFor.name: The seventy years
watchFor.thisFilm: Puts the plane into the ice on purpose with the dance still owed, and wakes up in a staged 1940s room that gets the ballgame wrong.
watchFor.future: Everything Steve does afterwards is coloured by having lost that life, right up to the point he goes back for it.

movies.title: Iron Man
movies.summary: A billionaire weapons manufacturer is captured and forced to build a weapon, but instead builds a suit of armor and escapes, setting him on a new path.

beforeWatch.context: Where the modern-day story actually starts, and the film everything else grew out of. Nothing before it is required. The two period pieces you have just watched are background colour rather than setup. Expect something fairly grounded: a film about weapons manufacturing and one man's very expensive change of heart.

deepDive.plot: Weapons manufacturer Tony Stark is captured by terrorists in Afghanistan and forced to build a weapon; instead, he secretly builds a suit of powered armor and escapes. Back home, he has a change of heart about his company's arms dealing, refines the suit into the Iron Man armor, and exposes and defeats his mentor Obadiah Stane, who tries to steal the technology and kill him.
deepDive.significance: The film that started all of it, and the one that set the house style: funny, fairly grounded, built around a personality rather than a plot. It also ends with the first post-credits scene, which turned out to be the most consequential thirty seconds in the whole run.
deepDive.orderNote: Third here, first in release order. Its present day is 2008, so it sits behind the 1940s film and the 1995 one, even though everything else was built outward from this.

watchFor.name: Tony Stark
watchFor.thisFilm: Sees his own products being used against American soldiers, and the entire arc is him refusing to un-see it. Most of the suit gets built in a cave with a box of scraps, which the film never lets him forget.

watchFor.name: Obadiah Stane
watchFor.thisFilm: His father's business partner, running the company from behind Tony's shoulder and arming both sides. The first MCU villain to be someone from the hero's own house.

watchFor.name: Pepper Potts
watchFor.thisFilm: Not a love interest so much as the only person Tony actually listens to, and the one who does the genuinely dangerous part of the third act.

watchFor.name: James Rhodes
watchFor.thisFilm: Tony's friend in the Air Force, in the difficult position of vouching for him professionally. Note the long look at the spare armour and the line about next time.
watchFor.future: He takes that suit in the next film.

watchFor.name: The arc reactor
watchFor.thisFilm: Keeping shrapnel out of his heart, which is the reason he wears it before it is the reason he can fly.

watchFor.name: "I am Iron Man"
watchFor.thisFilm: Goes off script at the press conference and tells the world, because the alternative is pretending to be someone else.
watchFor.future: No secret identity is why so much of what happens to him later happens in public.

watchFor.name: Nick Fury (post-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Waiting in the dark in Tony's house to say that Tony is not the only superhero in the world, and to mention something called the Avengers Initiative.
watchFor.future: The first thread of the team-up, four years before it pays off.

movies.title: The Incredible Hulk
movies.summary: A scientist on the run tries to control a rage-fueled transformation caused by a failed experiment, while the military hunts him down.

beforeWatch.context: Runs alongside the previous film rather than after it, and needs nothing from it. One heads-up that isn't a plot point: Bruce Banner is played by a different actor here than in every film that follows, which trips people up if nobody warns them. Treat it as a chase film. He's a fugitive when it opens, and the story is already in motion.

deepDive.plot: Scientist Bruce Banner, on the run and trying to cure the gamma radiation accident that turns him into the Hulk, is relentlessly hunted by the U.S. military under General Ross. After a confrontation with a soldier who injects himself with a similar serum and becomes the monstrous Abomination, Banner reluctantly transforms and defeats him, then goes into hiding, trying to control his condition.
deepDive.significance: The odd one out, and the least connected film in the run. What it does supply is the Hulk as a founding Avenger and Thaddeus Ross, who keeps turning up for the next fifteen years in steadily bigger jobs.
deepDive.orderNote: Fourth because it happens at roughly the same time as Iron Man, on the other side of the world, with no overlap until the last scene.

watchFor.name: Bruce is played by a different actor here
Bruce Banner
watchFor.thisFilm: Already on the run when it opens, counting days without an incident and learning breathing exercises. This is the only film that treats the Hulk purely as an illness.

watchFor.name: Thaddeus Ross
watchFor.thisFilm: Running the manhunt, and responsible for the experiment in the first place. He wants the weapon back rather than the man.
watchFor.future: Turns up as Secretary of State with the Sokovia Accords, and later as President.
watchFor.spoils: Captain America: Civil War/Captain America: Brave New World

watchFor.name: The super-soldier serum
watchFor.thisFilm: Ross was trying to recreate the 1940s programme, and the gamma accident was a by-product. It ties this film back to Captain America more tightly than anything on screen does.

watchFor.name: Emil Blonsky
watchFor.thisFilm: A soldier who wants what Banner has, takes a version of the serum, and becomes something worse than the thing he was hunting.
watchFor.future: Locked up for a very long time, then turns up in a cage fight and later a wellness retreat.
watchFor.spoils: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings/She-Hulk: Attorney at Law

watchFor.name: Samuel Sterns
watchFor.thisFilm: The scientist Bruce has been emailing for a cure, who takes gamma-infected blood into an open head wound and is left with a visibly swelling skull.
watchFor.future: A setup left sitting for sixteen years before Brave New World finally picked it up.

watchFor.name: Tony Stark (final scene)
watchFor.thisFilm: Walks into a bar to tell Ross a team is being put together. The tone is completely different from the rest of the film, and it is the first crossover the MCU ever did.
watchFor.future: Recontextualised later as Fury sending Tony in to be deliberately unhelpful.

movies.title: Iron Man 2
movies.summary: Facing pressure from the government and a personal crisis, a hero must deal with a new enemy seeking revenge tied to his father's past, while a former ally's ambitions grow.

beforeWatch.context: Picks up about six months after the first film, with Tony now a very public figure and enjoying it far too much. The wider organisation that has been hovering at the edges starts stepping properly into frame here, so this is the first film that feels like it's building toward something larger.

deepDive.plot: With his health failing from palladium poisoning caused by his own arc reactor, Tony Stark faces government pressure to hand over his suit technology, a vengeful new enemy named Ivan Vanko seeking payback for his father's mistreatment by Howard Stark, and a scheming rival arms dealer, Justin Hammer, who backs Vanko's attacks.
deepDive.significance: The film where S.H.I.E.L.D. stops hovering at the edges and walks into the plot. It introduces Natasha and puts Rhodey in a suit, and it is the first time the MCU visibly stops telling one story and starts building toward another one.
deepDive.orderNote: Follows Iron Man directly since it's a straightforward sequel continuing Tony's ongoing story a couple of years later.

watchFor.name: Tony is dying for most of this film
Natasha Romanoff
watchFor.thisFilm: Arrives as a legal assistant called Natalie Rushman and is a S.H.I.E.L.D. plant. The hallway fight is the first indication of what she actually does.
watchFor.future: Founding Avenger, and the whole Red Room question gets answered much later.

watchFor.name: James Rhodes
watchFor.thisFilm: Takes a suit rather than being given one, and the film is fairly clear that the military was always going to end up with one.
watchFor.future: War Machine from here on.

watchFor.name: Howard Stark's old film reels
watchFor.thisFilm: Tony finds a message from a father who could not say any of it to his face, plus a hidden element in a scale model of a fairground.
watchFor.future: Their relationship keeps getting revised, and Tony eventually gets to have the conversation properly.

watchFor.name: Ivan Vanko
watchFor.thisFilm: The son of a physicist Howard had deported. The film's argument is that the Starks made their enemies personally, one at a time.

watchFor.name: Justin Hammer
watchFor.thisFilm: A rival arms dealer who is desperate to be Tony and cannot manage it. Played straight enough to be funny.

watchFor.name: S.H.I.E.L.D. is running the film
watchFor.thisFilm: Fury has Tony's father's papers, an agent inside his company, and a file on him. By the end Tony is assessed as unsuitable for the team and recommended as a consultant.
watchFor.future: That assessment is why he is not recruited so much as tolerated in The Avengers.

watchFor.name: Mjolnir (post-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Coulson drives to New Mexico and finds a hammer in a crater.
watchFor.future: Straight into Thor.

movies.title: Thor
movies.summary: A powerful but arrogant warrior is cast out of his home realm and stripped of his power, learning humility on Earth while a threat brews back home.

beforeWatch.context: The first trip off Earth, and your introduction to Asgard: a realm with its own royal family, its own politics and a very long history, which these films treat as fact rather than myth. It works cold, and nothing from the previous films is needed. Once it reaches Earth it turns into a fish-out-of-water comedy for a while.

deepDive.plot: Arrogant Asgardian prince Thor is stripped of his power and banished to Earth by his father Odin as punishment for reigniting an ancient war. Humbled by his time among humans, he earns back his hammer Mjolnir and returns home just in time to stop his adopted brother Loki, who has seized the throne and nearly destroyed a rival realm to prove himself.
deepDive.significance: Opens the door to everything off-planet, and introduces Loki, who goes on to have a longer and stranger arc than almost anyone else in the saga. It also quietly establishes that the Infinity Stones are old news to somebody.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed sixth because its story wraps up right before The Avengers, with Loki's escape directly setting up that film's plot.

watchFor.name: Asgard as a place with politics
Thor
watchFor.thisFilm: Starts the film picking a fight that would restart a war, and gets thrown out for it. Whether he can lift the hammer is the entire measure of his character.

watchFor.name: Loki
watchFor.thisFilm: Finds out he was taken from Jotunheim as an infant and raised as a spare. Almost everything he does afterwards is a reply to that.
watchFor.future: Lets go of the bridge and turns up leading an invasion a year later.

watchFor.name: Odin
watchFor.thisFilm: Presented as wise and even-handed, though the film shows him doing several things that are neither.
watchFor.future: The truth about how Asgard was built gets revealed much later.

watchFor.name: Jane Foster
watchFor.thisFilm: An astrophysicist whose life's work is taken by S.H.I.E.L.D. in an afternoon. Her Einstein-Rosen bridge research is the reason any of this is on Earth.
watchFor.future: Off screen for a long stretch, and comes back to the story from a very different angle.

watchFor.name: Heimdall
watchFor.thisFilm: Sees and hears everything across the nine realms, and quietly decides when not to act on it.

watchFor.name: Hawkeye (cameo)
watchFor.thisFilm: A S.H.I.E.L.D. marksman in the rafters, asking whether he should slow Thor down. First sighting.
watchFor.future: Founding Avenger.

watchFor.name: Odin's vault
watchFor.thisFilm: The camera lingers on a case of relics during the tour. One of them is the Infinity Gauntlet, and the film does not stop to explain it.
watchFor.future: It is later established as a fake, which raises its own questions.

watchFor.name: The mid-credits scene
watchFor.thisFilm: Fury shows Selvig the Tesseract and calls it unlimited power. Selvig agrees, and Loki's reflection is standing behind him telling him to.
watchFor.future: Loki is already working on Earth before The Avengers begins, and is himself being steered by somebody else.

movies.title: The Avengers
movies.summary: A team of powerful individuals is assembled to stop a stolen artifact from being used to open a portal for an invading force.

beforeWatch.context: The payoff the whole phase has been quietly building toward, and the one film here that genuinely expects you to have done the reading. Everyone arrives with baggage from their own film and none of it gets re-explained. You'll get the most out of it if the four solo films are fresh, and if you remember that the organisation running the operation has been recruiting since the very first post-credits scene you saw.

deepDive.plot: After Loki steals the Tesseract and a mind-controlling scepter, Nick Fury assembles Iron Man, Captain America, Thor, Hulk, Black Widow, and Hawkeye to stop him before he can open a portal for an alien invasion force called the Chitauri. The team, initially fractured by ego and mistrust, comes together in New York to close the portal and defeat the invasion, cementing them as Earth's protectors.
deepDive.significance: The film that proved the whole idea worked. Six leads from five films in one story, none of them re-introduced, and it holds together. Every phase since has been built to end with something like it.
deepDive.orderNote: Last, because it is where the previous six films arrive. Loki, the Tesseract and every solo introduction land in the same story.

watchFor.name: How badly they get on at first
Phil Coulson
watchFor.thisFilm: The agent who has been in the background since the first film, used here as the reason the team stops arguing. Watch how deliberately Fury uses it afterwards.

watchFor.name: Bruce Banner
watchFor.thisFilm: Spends most of the film frightened of himself, and the secret turns out to be that he is always angry. This is the version of the character everything later is built on.

watchFor.name: Loki's sceptre
watchFor.thisFilm: Turns people, opens the portal, and is left with S.H.I.E.L.D. at the end. It works on everyone it touches except Tony, and only because it hits the arc reactor.
watchFor.future: There is a Mind Stone inside it, which becomes Vision and gives Wanda and Pietro their powers.

watchFor.name: Nick Fury lying to the Council
watchFor.thisFilm: Runs the operation on partial truths, including about what S.H.I.E.L.D. was building with the Tesseract. The Council's answer to the invasion is a nuclear missile.
watchFor.future: Both of those tell you what S.H.I.E.L.D. already is.

watchFor.name: The Chitauri and the wormhole
watchFor.thisFilm: The first alien invasion, and the reason New York gets referenced in almost every film afterwards. Tony flies a warhead through the portal not expecting to come back.

watchFor.name: The other one behind Loki
watchFor.thisFilm: The Other reports to a figure on a throne who smiles at what courting death would mean. A few seconds, no name given.
watchFor.future: That is Thanos, and he waits six years before doing it himself.

watchFor.name: What New York does to Tony
watchFor.thisFilm: Comes back through the portal having seen a fleet on the other side, and the film ends before he processes any of it.
watchFor.future: It becomes the anxiety driving Iron Man 3, and the reason he builds Ultron.

movies.title: Iron Man 3
movies.summary: In the aftermath of New York, Tony Stark grapples with anxiety while a terrorist calling himself the Mandarin targets him, drawing him into a conspiracy involving a rogue scientist's super-soldier program.

beforeWatch.context: Set at Christmas, roughly six months after the Battle of New York, and the first film to deal with the aftermath of that fight rather than the fight itself. Tony is not okay, and the film treats that as its actual subject. Everything you need about the invasion comes from the previous film.

deepDive.plot: Tony Stark, suffering panic attacks after the wormhole battle in New York, obsessively builds Iron Man suits while a terrorist calling himself the Mandarin bombs targets across the country. After his home is destroyed, Tony discovers the Mandarin is actually a washed-up actor, and the real threat is Aldrich Killian, a scientist using an unstable regenerative serum called Extremis to create super-soldiers, one of whom is Pepper Potts, kidnapped and injected. Tony destroys the Extremis operation, has the shrapnel and reactor removed from his chest, and quietly decides to stop defining himself by the suit.
deepDive.significance: Finishes what the first Iron Man started, by making Tony's dependence on the armour the actual subject rather than the fun part. It also plants the Mandarin as a fiction, which pays off a decade later in a completely different film.
deepDive.orderNote: Opens Phase Two because it's the first story to deal with life after The Avengers, picking up just months later at Christmas.

watchFor.name: Tony has not slept since New York
The panic attacks
watchFor.thisFilm: Anxiety attacks whenever New York comes up, and a workshop full of suits he built because he cannot stop. The film is fairly direct that the armour is the symptom.

watchFor.name: Extremis
watchFor.thisFilm: A regenerative treatment that makes people unstable enough to burn from the inside. It is also the first MCU story about a technology getting out rather than a person.

watchFor.name: Aldrich Killian
watchFor.thisFilm: A scientist Tony brushed off on a rooftop in 1999 and forgot about entirely. The film's argument is that Tony made this one himself, the same way his father made Vanko.

watchFor.name: Trevor Slattery
watchFor.thisFilm: The Mandarin turns out to be a hired actor with a drink problem, fronting a fiction built to give America a face to be frightened of. It annoyed a lot of people at the time.
watchFor.future: The real organisation abducts him for the insult, and he turns up decades later in a cage under Macau.
watchFor.spoils: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings

watchFor.name: Pepper Potts
watchFor.thisFilm: Dosed with Extremis and spends the last act doing the rescuing. Then asks him to stop.

watchFor.name: Happy Hogan
watchFor.thisFilm: Put in a coma early on, which is what makes it personal rather than geopolitical.

watchFor.name: The surgery
watchFor.thisFilm: Has the shrapnel taken out and drops the arc reactor into the sea. He does not need the suit any more, which is the point, and it does not last.
watchFor.future: By Age of Ultron the suits are back and there are a great many of them.

watchFor.name: Who Tony is talking to (post-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: The whole film has been narrated to Bruce Banner, who fell asleep at the start of it and is not a therapist.

movies.title: Thor: The Dark World
movies.summary: An ancient race led by the vengeful Malekith returns to plunge the universe into darkness using a weapon called the Aether, forcing Thor to make an uneasy alliance with Loki to save the Nine Realms.

beforeWatch.context: Thor has spent the time since New York putting out fires across the realms, and Asgard is dealing with the fallout of the first film's ending. Jane Foster has been off-screen the whole time and the film picks her thread back up. Both previous Thor-related films matter more than usual here.

deepDive.plot: An ancient race of Dark Elves led by Malekith awakens after millennia of dormancy, seeking to use a reality-warping substance called the Aether to plunge the universe back into darkness. When Jane Foster accidentally becomes host to the Aether, Malekith's forces attack Asgard and kill Thor's mother Frigga. Thor breaks Loki out of prison to smuggle Jane through the Nine Realms and defeat Malekith on Earth, at the cost of Asgard being left without its protective shield.
deepDive.significance: The least loved film in the run, and it still does two things that matter: it takes Thor's mother, which he is visibly still carrying six films later, and it puts a second Infinity Stone on the board while stating out loud that there are six.
deepDive.orderNote: Follows Iron Man 3 as the next Phase Two story chronologically, set in the same rough year.

watchFor.name: Loki in the cells
watchFor.thisFilm: Serving a sentence for New York, and the scenes between the two brothers are the reason people remember this one at all.

watchFor.name: Jane Foster
watchFor.thisFilm: Absorbs the Aether by accident, which makes her the plot rather than a participant in it. She and Thor separate not long after.
watchFor.future: Her exposure to it matters again much later, in a way nobody planned at the time.

watchFor.name: Frigga
watchFor.thisFilm: Thor's mother, who taught Loki everything he can do and is the only person in the family he does not lie to.
watchFor.future: Her death is what Thor is still carrying five films later, and he gets one more conversation with her.

watchFor.name: Heimdall
watchFor.thisFilm: Takes down a ship on foot, which is worth watching purely as a demonstration.

watchFor.name: The Aether
watchFor.thisFilm: Ancient, liquid, and behaving nothing like the glowing cubes so far. It is handed to a collector at the end rather than kept on Asgard, on the grounds that two stones in one vault is asking for trouble.
watchFor.future: It is the Reality Stone, and that reasoning turns out to be exactly wrong.

watchFor.name: The Collector (mid-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Takes the Aether and remarks that one down leaves five to go, which is the first time anyone on screen states there are six.
watchFor.future: You see his collection properly in Guardians of the Galaxy.

watchFor.name: Who is actually on the throne
watchFor.thisFilm: Odin sends Thor away with his blessing, and then the camera stays a moment too long. It is Loki, and he has been there for some time.
watchFor.future: Ragnarok opens by finding out how long, and what he did with it.

movies.title: Captain America: The Winter Soldier
movies.summary: Steve Rogers uncovers a conspiracy that has quietly taken root inside S.H.I.E.L.D. itself, and finds himself hunted by a mysterious, deadly assassin known as the Winter Soldier.

beforeWatch.context: Steve is two years into the present day now, working full time for the intelligence agency you have watched operate since the first film, and increasingly uneasy about how it does business. This is the most grounded, conspiracy-flavoured film so far, and it assumes you remember both his war-era history and who was running the show in New York.

deepDive.plot: Two years after the Battle of New York, Steve Rogers discovers that S.H.I.E.L.D. has been secretly infiltrated by Hydra from its very founding, using its own helicarriers and a predictive algorithm to preemptively eliminate future threats to Hydra's rule. Steve, Natasha, and new ally Sam Wilson uncover the conspiracy, only to find that the assassin hunting them, the Winter Soldier, is Steve's presumed-dead best friend Bucky Barnes, brainwashed by Hydra for decades. Steve refuses to fight him, the helicarriers are destroyed, and S.H.I.E.L.D. collapses entirely.
deepDive.significance: Probably the most consequential film in the run outside the Avengers ones. It takes S.H.I.E.L.D. off the board permanently, so every hero afterwards operates with no institution behind them, and it is the reason Civil War is about oversight at all.
deepDive.orderNote: Two years after The Avengers, which puts it in the same rough stretch as Iron Man 3 and The Dark World. It goes after both because what it does to S.H.I.E.L.D. changes the ground everything later stands on.

watchFor.name: Steve Rogers
watchFor.thisFilm: Working for an agency whose methods he does not agree with, and the film is largely about him deciding that loyalty to an institution is not the same as loyalty to what it claimed to stand for.

watchFor.name: Sam Wilson
watchFor.thisFilm: Introduced running the same loop and counselling veterans. Volunteers for all of it without needing to be persuaded, which is the whole character.
watchFor.future: The shield ends up with him, and this film is why that reads as earned.
watchFor.spoils: Avengers: Endgame/The Falcon and the Winter Soldier

watchFor.name: Nick Fury
watchFor.thisFilm: Ambushed in the street in broad daylight, and the film puts him on the back foot for the first time. His answer to distrust is a bigger gun, which is the thing being criticised.

watchFor.name: Project Insight
watchFor.thisFilm: Three helicarriers that can identify and kill people before they have done anything, sold as security. The film is unusually blunt that the technology is the problem regardless of who holds it.

watchFor.name: Sharon Carter
watchFor.thisFilm: Introduced as the neighbour, and is actually the agent assigned to watch him.
watchFor.future: The way she is treated afterwards is the seed of where she ends up.
watchFor.spoils: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier

watchFor.name: Who the Winter Soldier is
watchFor.thisFilm: Hydra's asset for seventy years, wiped after every mission, and it is Bucky. He pulls Steve out of the river without knowing why.
watchFor.future: Everything he does from here to Wakanda is about getting his own head back.

watchFor.name: What S.H.I.E.L.D. actually is
watchFor.thisFilm: Hydra never went away. It was rebuilt inside S.H.I.E.L.D. from the beginning, using the scientists brought over after the war, and the agency is dissolved once that is public.
watchFor.future: No safety net, no institution, no backup, for anybody, ever again.

watchFor.name: The twins (mid-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Two prisoners in a Hydra facility, one moving too fast to see and one moving objects without touching them, next to Loki's sceptre.
watchFor.future: Wanda and Pietro, and the sceptre is why they can do it.

movies.title: Guardians of the Galaxy
movies.summary: A group of misfit outlaws from across the galaxy is forced to band together to stop a fanatical warrior from acquiring a mysterious orb of immense and destructive power.

beforeWatch.context: A hard reset into a completely different corner of the universe, with a new cast who have never heard of anyone you've met so far. You can watch it cold, since it explains its own world from scratch. The only thread connecting it to what you've seen is one object that behaves a lot like others you've encountered before.

deepDive.plot: Small-time thief Peter Quill, abducted from Earth as a child, steals a mysterious orb that turns out to be an Infinity Stone, drawing the attention of the fanatical Kree warrior Ronan. Quill is forced into an uneasy alliance with the assassin Gamora, the bounty hunters Rocket and Groot, and the vengeful Drax, and together they narrowly stop Ronan from using the Stone to destroy an entire planet, forming an unlikely family in the process.
deepDive.significance: Opens up the rest of the universe with a cast who have never heard of the Avengers, and proves the MCU could work without them. It also gives Thanos his first real scene, and leaves a stone somewhere he can simply go and take it.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed here as the first fully cosmic MCU story, set in the same broad period as the Earth-based Phase Two films.

watchFor.name: Peter Quill
watchFor.thisFilm: Taken off Earth as a child the night his mother died, and has been performing a version of himself ever since. The Walkman is the only thing he has left of her.

watchFor.name: Gamora
watchFor.thisFilm: Thanos took her as a child after killing half her planet, and raised her as a weapon. She is trying to defect from the start.
watchFor.future: What Thanos did to her, and what he does with her, is the emotional centre of Infinity War.

watchFor.name: Nebula
watchFor.thisFilm: Rebuilt piece by piece every time she lost to Gamora. Almost nothing about her is voluntary yet.
watchFor.future: She has the longest and quietest redemption in the saga.

watchFor.name: Drax
watchFor.thisFilm: Everything is literal, and the joke works because the grief underneath it is real. His family were killed by Ronan.

watchFor.name: Rocket and Groot
watchFor.thisFilm: Rocket is an experiment nobody asked to make, and is angry about it in a way the film only hints at here.
watchFor.future: Vol. 3 shows you exactly what was done to him.

watchFor.name: Ronan the Accuser
watchFor.thisFilm: A Kree fanatic operating outside a peace treaty he never agreed to, working for Thanos until he decides he does not have to.
watchFor.future: You meet him earlier in his career, and in better standing, in Captain Marvel.

watchFor.name: Thanos
watchFor.thisFilm: First proper appearance, sitting on the throne and lending out his daughters. He is presented as an employer here rather than a threat.
watchFor.future: Both daughters end up on the other side of him.

watchFor.name: The Orb
watchFor.thisFilm: Cracks open to reveal a stone that destroys anyone who touches it alone, and is handed to the Nova Corps on Xandar for safekeeping.
watchFor.future: The Power Stone, and Xandar is the first place Thanos goes.

watchFor.name: Yondu
watchFor.thisFilm: Was paid to deliver Peter to his father and kept him instead, and will not say why.
watchFor.future: The reason is the whole of Vol. 2.

movies.title: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2
movies.summary: Shortly after escaping other galactic factions, the Guardians must survive the appearance of Peter Quill's mysterious birth father while old grudges within the team come to a head. Set only months after the first film, so it's grouped here narratively even though it released during Phase Three.

beforeWatch.context: A couple of months after the first film, with the same crew now working together, badly, as a going concern. It's almost entirely self-contained: no knowledge of Earth's heroes is needed, and the film is much more interested in this crew's family history than in the wider universe.

movies.timeSkip: A few months after the first Guardians film

deepDive.plot: Months after saving the galaxy, the Guardians are hired by the golden Sovereign race, whom they quickly anger, and rescued by a mysterious being who claims to be Peter Quill's father, Ego, a Celestial. Peter is drawn in by the promise of a family and cosmic power, but discovers Ego has been systematically seeding planets with his own offspring and hollowing out worlds (including killing his own children) to eventually reshape the universe in his image. The Guardians kill Ego together, and Peter chooses his found family over his birth father.
deepDive.significance: The middle film of the trilogy and the one carrying its argument: that the people who raised you count for more than the ones who made you. Yondu's ending is the best thing in any of the three.
deepDive.orderNote: Sits in Phase Two because it happens a few months after the first film, in 2014, even though it came out in 2017. Story order over release branding, the same call made for Captain Marvel and Black Widow.

watchFor.name: It is a film about fathers
Ego
watchFor.thisFilm: Peter's father, a Celestial who has been seeding planets for millions of years and needs a second Celestial to finish the job. He killed Peter's mother deliberately.
watchFor.future: Celestials come back much bigger in Eternals.

watchFor.name: Yondu
watchFor.thisFilm: Kept Peter because he knew what Ego did to the other children. Gives Peter the only spacesuit and says he was his father, which is the film's whole argument in one line.
watchFor.future: Kraglin inherits the fin and spends two films learning to use the arrow.

watchFor.name: Mantis
watchFor.thisFilm: An empath kept by Ego to help him sleep, with no experience of being treated as a person. Her scenes with Drax are the film's best running joke.

watchFor.name: Nebula and Gamora
watchFor.thisFilm: The film stops for their argument about which of them was actually the victim, and it recontextualises the first film entirely.

watchFor.name: Kraglin
watchFor.thisFilm: Sides with Yondu against the mutiny, and ends the film holding the fin.

watchFor.name: Groot
watchFor.thisFilm: Regrown from a cutting and is a different person, which the film treats as a bereavement everybody is being polite about.
watchFor.future: Grows into the sullen teenager seen in Infinity War.

watchFor.name: Adam Warlock's cocoon (post-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Ayesha, humiliated, unveils a cocoon holding something she has built to destroy the Guardians.
watchFor.future: He does not actually appear until Vol. 3, six years later.

postCredit.timing: The five scenes are scattered throughout the credits rather than bunched at the start or end — check back periodically instead of waiting for one big moment at the very finish.

movies.title: Avengers: Age of Ultron
movies.summary: Tony Stark's attempt to build a peacekeeping artificial intelligence backfires when it becomes the villainous Ultron, forcing the Avengers to confront a new threat alongside a pair of enhanced siblings.

beforeWatch.context: The team is back together and has been running as a unit for a while when this opens. It drops you into an ongoing campaign rather than assembling anyone. It leans on the collapse of the organisation from The Winter Soldier and on Tony's state of mind after Iron Man 3, so both are worth having fresh.

deepDive.plot: A year after Winter Soldier, the Avengers raid a Hydra base and recover Loki's scepter, inside which Tony Stark and Bruce Banner discover an artificial intelligence they use to build a global peacekeeping program, Ultron. Ultron immediately concludes humanity itself is the threat to peace and tries to trigger an extinction-level event using a floating city and a vibranium-powered synthetic body. The Avengers, aided by two enhanced Hydra experiments (Wanda and Pietro Maximoff), stop Ultron, though Pietro is killed and a new synthetic being, Vision, is created from the very body Ultron built for himself.
deepDive.significance: The last time the original six work as one team without reservations. It introduces Vision and Wanda, and it hands Tony the mistake that Civil War then makes everyone else pay for.
deepDive.orderNote: Caps the Phase Two Avengers-adjacent storylines a year after Winter Soldier, directly before the roster shakeup of Civil War.

watchFor.name: They have been working as a unit for a while
Ultron
watchFor.thisFilm: Tony builds a peacekeeping intelligence out of the Mind Stone without telling anyone, and it decides within seconds that peace means no people. He is Tony's fear given a body.

watchFor.name: Wanda and Pietro Maximoff
watchFor.thisFilm: Volunteers from Sokovia who lost their parents to a Stark shell, which is why they start on Ultron's side. Wanda's visions are what actually breaks the team.
watchFor.future: Wanda's grief becomes the subject of an entire series.

watchFor.name: Vision
watchFor.thisFilm: Made from Ultron's intended body, JARVIS, and the Mind Stone. Lifting the hammer is the film settling the question of whether to trust him.
watchFor.future: The stone in his forehead is the last one Thanos needs.

watchFor.name: Ulysses Klaue
watchFor.thisFilm: An arms dealer with stolen vibranium and a brand on his neck reading thief, put there by a country nobody talks about.
watchFor.future: That country and that brand are the starting point of Black Panther.

watchFor.name: Thor's vision
watchFor.thisFilm: Goes to a cave to see what Wanda showed him and comes back talking about the stones as a pattern rather than a coincidence. He is the first Avenger to work out that something is arranging them.

watchFor.name: Clint's farmhouse
watchFor.thisFilm: The reveal that Hawkeye has a wife, children and a house nobody knew about, which is what the five years later cost him.
watchFor.future: It is why he becomes Ronin.

watchFor.name: Who does not survive
watchFor.thisFilm: Pietro is shot taking a burst of fire meant for Clint and a child, having spent the film being written off.
watchFor.future: Wanda feels him die from across the city, and it is the first of the losses that eventually makes Westview.

watchFor.name: The Gauntlet (mid-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Thanos takes the glove out of a cabinet and says he will do it himself, having spent three films hiring people.
watchFor.future: He is not exaggerating.

movies.title: Doctor Strange
movies.summary: A brilliant but arrogant surgeon loses the use of his hands in an accident and seeks healing in the mystic arts, discovering a hidden world of sorcery and a looming threat from another dimension.

beforeWatch.context: A standalone origin story that opens the door on magic, which the films have not seriously dealt with until now. Nothing prior is required. It runs roughly parallel to the films around it rather than after them, so don't worry about slotting it precisely.

deepDive.plot: Brilliant but arrogant surgeon Stephen Strange loses the use of his hands in a car accident and, out of desperation, seeks out a mystical order in Kathmandu led by the Ancient One. He masters the mystic arts faster than anyone before him, only to discover a rogue former student, Kaecilius, is trying to merge Earth with a dark dimension ruled by the entity Dormammu. Strange traps Dormammu in a time loop using the Time Stone to force a bargain, saving Earth and choosing to become the new Sorcerer Supreme.
deepDive.significance: Puts magic on the board as something with rules, costs and a bureaucracy, and gives Earth a second Infinity Stone with someone standing over it. Strange goes from a new character to one of the two or three people the ending depends on.
deepDive.orderNote: Set the same year as Civil War, but its story is self-contained, so it's placed here as a natural thematic grouping within Phase Three rather than a tight timeline link.

watchFor.name: Stephen Strange
watchFor.thisFilm: A surgeon whose hands are ruined, who goes to Kathmandu for a cure and stays for something else. He is arrogant in the same register as Tony Stark, deliberately.

watchFor.name: The Ancient One
watchFor.thisFilm: Teaches him, and is drawing power from the Dark Dimension to stay alive while forbidding everyone else from doing the same. The film lets that stand as a real failing rather than explaining it away.
watchFor.future: Strange goes back and meets her again during the time heist.

watchFor.name: Wong
watchFor.thisFilm: Librarian, straight man, and the one who takes the rules seriously.
watchFor.future: Ends up running the whole order, and turns up everywhere.

watchFor.name: Karl Mordo
watchFor.thisFilm: The true believer, and the film is careful that he is not wrong. He leaves at the end because the people around him kept breaking their own laws and winning.
watchFor.future: The post-credits has him draining a sorcerer's power and saying there are too many. It has gone nowhere so far.

watchFor.name: The Time Stone
watchFor.thisFilm: Sits in the Eye of Agamotto, and Strange wins the film by trapping a cosmic entity in a loop rather than by fighting it. Beating something by being willing to die repeatedly is a good measure of him.
watchFor.future: Hands it over to save one life, which is either a mistake or the plan.

watchFor.name: Thor (mid-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Turns up in the Sanctum asking for help finding Odin, with a bottomless beer.
watchFor.future: Straight into Ragnarok's opening.

movies.title: Ant-Man
movies.summary: Con man Scott Lang is recruited by scientist Hank Pym to master a suit that lets him shrink to the size of an insect, using his new ability to pull off a heist that could save the world.

beforeWatch.context: A deliberately small film: a heist story about one family, set in a world where the big team exists but is busy elsewhere. It stands alone almost completely, and it is the first film in a while that is not about saving the planet. A little familiarity with the wider world helps one or two jokes land, and nothing more than that.

deepDive.plot: Recently released ex-con Scott Lang is recruited by scientist Hank Pym to become the new Ant-Man, using a size-changing suit Pym has kept hidden for decades. Pym's plan is to stop his former protégé, Darren Cross, from replicating and weaponizing the same shrinking technology as the Yellowjacket. Scott pulls off a heist inside Cross's own company, defeats Yellowjacket, and earns Hank's trust, while Hank's daughter Hope is finally given her mother's old Wasp suit.
deepDive.significance: A deliberate step down in scale after Age of Ultron, and the film nobody expected to matter. It plants the Quantum Realm, which turns out to be the mechanism the Avengers use to undo the Snap.
deepDive.orderNote: Sits early in Phase Three, shortly after Age of Ultron, as the smallest story in the run. The mid-credits fight with Sam is what puts Scott in Germany a year later.

watchFor.name: It is a heist film, not a superhero one
Scott Lang
watchFor.thisFilm: An electrical engineer with a burglary conviction, trying to make child support so he can see his daughter. Lower stakes than anything around it, on purpose.

watchFor.name: Hank Pym
watchFor.thisFilm: The original Ant-Man, who walked away from S.H.I.E.L.D. when he found out what they wanted the technology for. Watch how much he is not telling Hope.

watchFor.name: Hope van Dyne
watchFor.thisFilm: Better qualified than Scott for the entire film, and says so. Her father's refusal to let her wear the suit is about her mother.
watchFor.future: She gets the suit in the post-credits and is the Wasp from then on.

watchFor.name: Luis
watchFor.thisFilm: The story-within-a-story bits are doing real work, not just filling time.

watchFor.name: The Quantum Realm
watchFor.thisFilm: Scott goes subatomic and comes back, which Hank says should be impossible. The film treats it as a near-death experience rather than a location.
watchFor.future: It becomes the mechanism for the time heist, so this scene is load-bearing for the whole saga.

watchFor.name: What happened to Janet
watchFor.thisFilm: Hank's wife went subatomic to disarm a missile and never came back. He believes she is simply gone.
watchFor.future: She is not gone, and she has been down there thirty years.

watchFor.name: Falcon (mid-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Scott breaks into the Avengers compound for a piece of kit and gets into a fight with Sam, who decides not to mention it.
watchFor.future: It is why Sam calls him for the airport.

movies.title: Captain America: Civil War
movies.summary: A government oversight act splits the Avengers into two factions, pitting Captain America and his allies against Iron Man's, while a hidden mastermind quietly manipulates the conflict from the shadows.

beforeWatch.context: The consequences film. Two of the previous films ended with a city badly damaged and a lot of civilians caught in the middle, and the world's governments have finally decided to do something about oversight. It expects you to remember both incidents, and to remember who Steve's oldest friend is and what happened to him.

deepDive.plot: After an Avengers mission in Lagos causes civilian casualties, the United Nations proposes the Sokovia Accords, an oversight framework for enhanced individuals, which splits the team between Tony Stark's faction, who support regulation, and Steve Rogers', who do not. The rift explodes into open conflict when Bucky Barnes is framed for a bombing at the Accords signing, and Zemo, a grieving Sokovian whose family died in Ultron's battle, manipulates both sides into an airport battle, then reveals that a brainwashed Bucky killed Tony's parents years earlier.
deepDive.significance: The break that never really heals. It scatters the team for years, puts Steve underground, introduces Black Panther and Spider-Man in the same film, and leaves Tony and Steve not speaking, which is exactly how Thanos finds them.
deepDive.orderNote: Opens Phase Three as the direct fallout of Age of Ultron's collateral damage, about a year later.

watchFor.name: Nobody in this is entirely wrong
The Sokovia Accords
watchFor.thisFilm: Government oversight of enhanced people, brought by Ross, and the film splits the team on it rather than on a villain. Tony agrees because of a mother in a lift; Steve refuses because of what the last institution turned out to be.

watchFor.name: T'Challa
watchFor.thisFilm: Becomes king in the middle of a bombing that kills his father, and spends the film hunting the wrong man. The one person here who chooses to stop.
watchFor.future: Straight into his own film, days later.

watchFor.name: Peter Parker
watchFor.thisFilm: Fifteen, recruited out of a Queens bedroom by a billionaire who does not tell his aunt what the internship is. The suit is a bribe.
watchFor.future: Homecoming picks up two months later.

watchFor.name: Helmut Zemo
watchFor.thisFilm: Not enhanced, not powerful, and he wins. Lost his family in Sokovia and works out that the Avengers can be made to do it to themselves.
watchFor.future: Comes back years later, out of prison and no less clever.
watchFor.spoils: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier

watchFor.name: Vision and Wanda
watchFor.thisFilm: The first film to treat them as a pairing rather than teammates, and it is where the containment of her begins.
watchFor.future: It is the relationship WandaVision is built on top of.

watchFor.name: What Zemo actually has
watchFor.thisFilm: Not a weapon. A recording of the Winter Soldier killing Howard and Maria Stark in 1991, played to Tony in front of Steve, who already knew.
watchFor.future: Nothing between Tony and Steve is repaired before Infinity War, and it is the last thing standing between them in Endgame.

watchFor.name: Bucky Barnes
watchFor.thisFilm: Framed for the bombing, still triggerable by a list of words, and asks to go back under until it can be fixed.
watchFor.future: Shuri fixes it, and Wakanda is where he spends the gap.

movies.title: Black Widow
movies.summary: A fugitive in the fallout of Civil War, Natasha Romanoff is forced to confront dangerous ties from her past when a mysterious figure threatens to unravel the Red Room program that trained her. Released in Phase Four but set in 2016, so it's grouped here narratively, same reasoning as Captain Marvel and Guardians Vol. 2.

beforeWatch.context: Set immediately after the previous film, in the window where Natasha is a fugitive with nowhere to go. It's a prequel to everything that comes after it in this list, and it finally goes back to the history she has been alluding to since her very first appearance. Released years later, so expect a modern look on an older point in the story.

movies.timeSkip: Set right after Civil War, even though it released in 2021

deepDive.plot: On the run after Civil War, Natasha Romanoff is drawn back into her past when her 'sister' Yelena Belova resurfaces with a chemical weapon that can free Black Widow operatives from their mind control. The two team up with their former 'family', the super-soldier Alexei and the spy Melina, to take down the Red Room and its leader, Dreykov. They free dozens of brainwashed assassins, and Yelena gets a version of the escape Natasha made for herself years earlier.
deepDive.significance: The only real look at Natasha's backstory before her death in Endgame, and it hands her legacy directly to Yelena, who becomes an ongoing character across Hawkeye and beyond.
deepDive.orderNote: Set in 2016, directly after Civil War, so it's grouped here narratively rather than by its actual 2021 release.

watchFor.name: Natasha Romanoff
watchFor.thisFilm: On the run after Civil War, which is the gap this film fills. It is the only one that treats her as the lead rather than the team's connective tissue.
watchFor.future: Released after Endgame, so it is a film about someone the audience already knows is gone.

watchFor.name: Yelena Belova
watchFor.thisFilm: Raised in the same fake family and put through the same programme, and she is funnier and angrier about all of it. The vest conversation is the best scene in the film.
watchFor.future: Takes the name, and turns up hunting Clint two years later.

watchFor.name: The fake family in Ohio
watchFor.thisFilm: The three-year childhood was an undercover operation, and the film keeps sitting in how much of it was real anyway.

watchFor.name: Alexei Shostakov
watchFor.thisFilm: The Red Guardian, the Soviet answer to Captain America, mostly used for comedy and occasionally not.
watchFor.future: On Valentina's team later, still talking about the old days.

watchFor.name: Melina
watchFor.thisFilm: The scientist who built the chemical conditioning, and knows exactly what she did.

watchFor.name: The Red Room
watchFor.thisFilm: Answers what Natasha meant by the red in her ledger, and frees the widows still in it rather than only settling her own account.

watchFor.name: Valentina (post-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Turns up at Natasha's grave to point Yelena at Clint, telling her he is responsible.
watchFor.future: That lie is the engine of the Hawkeye series, and the first move of the team she is quietly building.

postCredit.skipNote: Skip this movie's credit scene if you're following narrative order. It's set after her Endgame, which you haven't watched yet at this point. Come back and watch it right before Hawkeye, S1 Disney+.

movies.title: Black Panther
movies.summary: After his father's death, T'Challa returns to the technologically advanced nation of Wakanda to claim the throne, but a challenger with ties to his family's past threatens both his crown and Wakanda's secrets.

beforeWatch.context: Picks up only days after the last film, with T'Challa heading home to take the throne after events there. Wakanda gets built from the ground up for you and nothing about it is assumed, but the reason he is going home, and grieving, comes straight out of the previous film.

movies.timeSkip: Set only days after Civil War, though released two years later

deepDive.plot: Following his father's death in Civil War, T'Challa returns to Wakanda to be crowned king, only to be challenged for the throne by Erik Killmonger, an estranged cousin raised in America who was abandoned by Wakanda after his own father's death decades earlier. Killmonger briefly seizes the throne and plans to arm oppressed people worldwide with Wakandan weapons, forcing T'Challa to reclaim his birthright and choose a new path of engaging with the world rather than hiding from it.
deepDive.significance: Ends with Wakanda giving up the secrecy it was built on, which changes its place in every film afterwards. It also introduces Shuri and Okoye, and Killmonger, who is still the villain most people name first.
deepDive.orderNote: Set only days after Civil War, so it's placed right behind it even though it released two years later.

watchFor.name: Wakanda has been hiding on purpose
T'Challa
watchFor.thisFilm: Inherits a country built on a policy he starts the film agreeing with and ends it rejecting. Unusually for a superhero film, the hero concedes the villain's argument.

watchFor.name: Erik Killmonger
watchFor.thisFilm: T'Challa's cousin, abandoned in Oakland after his father was killed by T'Challa's. His grievance is legitimate and his method is not, and the film refuses to simplify either.
watchFor.future: Widely rated one of the best villains in the run, and the reason Wakanda opens up.

watchFor.name: Shuri
watchFor.thisFilm: Runs Wakanda's entire research programme at sixteen and is funnier than her brother.
watchFor.future: Ends up carrying far more than anyone intended.

watchFor.name: Okoye
watchFor.thisFilm: Loyal to the throne rather than the person on it, which the film makes genuinely costly for her.

watchFor.name: Nakia
watchFor.thisFilm: Has been arguing for intervention since before the film starts, and is proved right.

watchFor.name: M'Baku
watchFor.thisFilm: Introduced as a threat, and turns into the person who does the decent thing when nobody is watching.

watchFor.name: Ulysses Klaue
watchFor.thisFilm: The vibranium thief from Age of Ultron, finally the subject of a plot rather than a loose end, and dispatched halfway through to make room for the real one.

watchFor.name: Bucky (post-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Waking up in a Wakandan village, fixed, being called the White Wolf by the local children.
watchFor.future: That is where Infinity War finds him.

movies.title: Spider-Man: Homecoming
movies.summary: Still adjusting to his new abilities, Peter Parker balances high school life with his growing responsibilities as Spider-Man while facing a black-market arms dealer wielding stolen alien technology.

beforeWatch.context: A few months after the airport fight, told from the point of view of the fifteen-year-old who was briefly flown in for it and then sent home. This is a high-school film first and a superhero film second. You need the previous film for how he got the suit, and very little else.

movies.timeSkip: A few months after Civil War

deepDive.plot: Still buzzing from the Avengers' Berlin airport battle, Peter Parker juggles high school with amateur superheroics, eager for Tony Stark to call him up for real missions. When he stumbles onto a black-market arms operation run by Adrian Toomes (the Vulture), selling weapons built from salvaged Chitauri and Avengers-battle technology, Peter's over-eagerness nearly gets people killed, forcing him to learn responsibility the hard way before defeating Toomes without Iron Man's help.
deepDive.significance: Reboots Spider-Man within the MCU's own continuity, deepens Peter's mentor/mentee relationship with Tony, and plants a 'salvaged alien tech' black market that recurs in later Spider-Man films.
deepDive.orderNote: Set a couple of months after Civil War, continuing straight from Peter's MCU debut there.

watchFor.name: It is a high school film
Peter Parker
watchFor.thisFilm: Fifteen and desperate to be called up, which is the whole engine. He is not a tragic figure yet, and the film is much lighter than either previous Spider-Man series.

watchFor.name: Tony Stark
watchFor.thisFilm: A bad mentor doing his best, largely absent, communicating through Happy. Taking the suit back is the closest he comes to actual parenting.
watchFor.future: What Peter is trying to live up to changes completely two films later.

watchFor.name: Adrian Toomes
watchFor.thisFilm: A salvage contractor put out of business when Stark's people took over the New York clean-up. The car journey is the best scene in the film and neither of them raises their voice.
watchFor.future: Kept alive in prison, and he does not give Peter up.

watchFor.name: Salvaged Chitauri technology
watchFor.thisFilm: The weapons are all built from things left behind by the alien invasion, which is the first time the MCU treats its own wreckage as an economy.
watchFor.future: That black market keeps turning up.

watchFor.name: Ned and MJ
watchFor.thisFilm: Ned finds out in the first act. Michelle is barely in it and is watching everything.
watchFor.future: Both of them matter enormously by the end of the trilogy.

watchFor.name: Who Liz's father turns out to be
watchFor.thisFilm: He opens the front door in a dinner jacket to drive his daughter's date to the dance, and works it out in about ninety seconds.

watchFor.name: Turning down the Avengers
watchFor.thisFilm: Offered a place on the team and says no, because he would rather stay local. It is the moment the film argues he has earned it.

movies.title: Ant-Man and the Wasp
movies.summary: Scott Lang juggles house arrest with a new mission alongside Hope van Dyne and Hank Pym to rescue Hope's mother, Janet, from the mysterious and dangerous Quantum Realm.

beforeWatch.context: Scott is under house arrest for taking part in the airport fight, and the film is a light, self-contained caper, put there deliberately as a breather. Important placement note: it runs alongside the previous film rather than after it, and only catches up to that film's ending in its final moments.

movies.timeSkip: Set concurrently with, right up to, Infinity War's ending

deepDive.plot: Still under house arrest after Civil War, Scott Lang is pulled back into Hank Pym and Hope van Dyne's world when they need his unique Quantum Realm experience to rescue Hope's mother, Janet, who's been trapped there for three decades. Their efforts to build a working tunnel into the Quantum Realm are complicated by a black-market tech dealer and a mysterious, phasing woman named Ghost, who needs Janet's quantum energy to stabilize her own condition. They retrieve Janet just as the Snap disintegrates half the universe outside, Hope, Hank and Janet included, which leaves Scott alone and stranded in the Quantum Realm.
deepDive.significance: Introduces the Quantum Realm mechanics in enough depth that it becomes the literal basis for the time-travel plan in Endgame, and its ending directly explains Scott's mysterious absence at the start of that film.
deepDive.orderNote: Set concurrently with Infinity War's climax, explaining what the Ant-Man family was doing while the Snap happened elsewhere.

watchFor.name: The lightest film either side of it
Where Scott is
watchFor.thisFilm: Two years of house arrest for the airport in Germany, with an ankle tag and three days left. That is the price of Civil War for someone without a legal team.

watchFor.name: Hope van Dyne
watchFor.thisFilm: In the suit from the start and better at it than Scott, which the film treats as settled rather than remarkable.

watchFor.name: Janet van Dyne
watchFor.thisFilm: Found alive after thirty years subatomic, having adapted to it in ways the film does not fully explain.
watchFor.future: What she was doing down there, and who she met, gets answered much later.

watchFor.name: Ghost
watchFor.thisFilm: A villain who is in constant pain and wants to stop being in pain. Nobody in the film is really an antagonist.

watchFor.name: The Quantum Realm, properly
watchFor.thisFilm: Mapped, entered deliberately, and explained in enough detail to function as a place rather than an accident.
watchFor.future: Every rule established here is what the time heist runs on.

watchFor.name: When this actually happens
watchFor.thisFilm: Runs alongside Infinity War rather than after it. The credits scene is the Snap arriving mid-experiment, which is why it sits here in the order.
watchFor.future: Scott stuck in the Quantum Realm is exactly where Endgame finds him.

postCredit.timing: The mid-credit scene plays fairly early; the real post-credit scene (Scott stranded and alone) doesn't hit until after the full cast and crew crawl, so it's easy to miss if you stop early.
postCredit.skipNote: Skip both credit scenes if you're following the narative order! Come back after Infinity War.

movies.title: Thor: Ragnarok
movies.summary: Imprisoned on the other side of the universe, Thor must race home to stop the fire demon Surtur and his ruthless sister Hela from destroying Asgard, teaming up with the Hulk and a band of misfits along the way.

beforeWatch.context: Thor has spent two years off-screen chasing the thread he walked away on at the end of Age of Ultron, and comes back to find things at home very different. A hard swerve into comedy compared with the previous two, and that is deliberate. Both earlier Thor films and Age of Ultron feed directly into where he is when it opens.

deepDive.plot: Imprisoned across the universe by the Grandmaster on the trash-planet Sakaar, Thor must escape and race home after learning his long-hidden older sister, Hela, the Goddess of Death, has seized Asgard's throne and set her sights on galactic conquest. Reluctantly teaming up with an exiled Valkyrie, a captive Hulk, and a scheming Loki, Thor allows the fire demon Surtur to destroy Asgard entirely rather than let Hela keep it, saving his people, now refugees, at the cost of his home.
deepDive.significance: A tonal reinvention of the Thor franchise that nonetheless ends in real tragedy, the loss of Asgard, and directly sets up Thanos's attack at the very start of Infinity War.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed here as the last calm-before-the-storm story before Infinity War, with its ending flowing directly into that film's opening scene.

watchFor.name: A comedy, until it very much is not
Thor

movies.title: Avengers: Infinity War
movies.summary: The Avengers and their allies unite to stop the Mad Titan Thanos from collecting all six Infinity Stones and using them to wipe out half of all life in the universe.

beforeWatch.context: This is the film that every film so far has been leading up to. This movie moves between Earth and deep space constantly, and expects you to already know the cosmic crew, the state of Wakanda, where the team stands after Civil War, and what the various coloured stones people keep chasing actually are. Keep a mental tally of the stones we already know about: Space Stone (Tesseract): Last seen on Asgard - Mind Stone: On Earth, embedded in Vision's forehead - Time Stone (Eye of Agamotto): Around Strange's neck in New York - Reality Stone (Aether): Left with the Collector on Knowhere - Power Stone: Locked away on Xandar in a Nova Corps vault - Soul Stone: No one knows its location.

movies.timeSkip: Directly after the mid-credit scene of Thor: Ragnarok

deepDive.plot: Thanos, having gathered several Infinity Stones already, launches an assault across the galaxy to collect the rest, including the Mind Stone from Vision's forehead and the Time Stone from Doctor Strange, so he can snap away half of all life in the universe to 'balance' it. Despite the combined efforts of nearly every hero introduced across a decade of films, Thanos succeeds, and the film ends with half of all life, including many beloved heroes, disintegrating into dust.
deepDive.significance: Where a decade of Infinity Stone setup arrives at once. It is also the first film in the run where the villain simply wins, and the ending is played straight rather than walked back before the credits.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed near the end of Phase Three as the direct payoff of a decade of Infinity Stone setups across nearly every prior film.

watchFor.name: The Snap

postCredit.skipNote: Make sure to go back and watch the Ant-Man and the Wasp post-credit scene after this movie if you're following the narrative order, as it takes place after the events of Infinity War.

movies.title: Captain Marvel
movies.summary: The story follows Vers as she transforms into one of the most powerful heroes in the universe. When a huge space war between two alien groups ends up coming to Earth, she and a small group of friends find themselves trapped right in the middle of the chaos.

beforeWatch.context: Set in 1995, half a century after the WWII film and over a decade before the present day story starts. Watch for younger versions of Fury and Coulson. This takes place long before they became high-ranking S.H.I.E.L.D. figures we know from The Avengers.

deepDive.plot: Set in the mid-1990s, an amnesiac Kree soldier named Vers discovers she's actually Carol Danvers, a former U.S. Air Force pilot who gained cosmic powers from an alien energy core. Along the way she uncovers that the 'enemy' Skrulls she's been hunting are actually refugees, and that her own Kree allies have been lying to her for years. She helps the Skrulls find a new home and leaves Earth to help them resettle across the galaxy.
deepDive.significance: Introduces one of the MCU's most powerful heroes and recontextualizes Nick Fury's early career. It stands almost entirely on its own. What it's quietly doing is filling in the era before any of the heroes existed, back when the organisation that eventually assembles them was a much smaller outfit. It seeds two long-term threads: the Tesseract's origins and the Skrulls' true nature, both of which pay off years later. The mid-credits scene jumps straight from 1995 into the immediate aftermath of Infinity War, showing the remaining Avengers gathered around the pager Fury sent. It's also revealed that the Avengers' name was inspired by Carol's Air Force call sign, 'Avenger.'
deepDive.orderNote: Chronologically this film could be placed after Captain America: The First Avenger, but narratively this is the best place to have it. This film matches the intergalactic setting the surrounding films have, rather than placing it right after a more grounded WWII movie. This film also sets up the pager that Nick Fury uses to call Captain Marvel in Endgame, so it makes sense to place it right before Endgame.

watchFor.name: Tesseract
watchFor.thisFilm: The last time we saw it chronologically was in Captain America: The First Avenger, when it fell into the ocean. At the end of the film we see Goose regurgitate it explaining how S.H.I.E.L.D. has it in The Avengers.

watchFor.name: The Skrulls
watchFor.thisFilm: Introduce the Skrulls as a distinct alien race with their own culture and motivations. They're not conquerors, but are actually refugees fleeing Kree genocide.
watchFor.future: Sets up the Skrull-Kree conflict that will play out in later films.

watchFor.name: Ronan the Accuser's Rank
watchFor.thisFilm: When we met him in Guardians of the Galaxy, he was a rogue Kree extremist. In this movie, he is still an official high-ranking military leader.

watchFor.name: Planet Hala

watchFor.name: The Supreme Intelligence
watchFor.future: Carol Danvers later returns to Hala to destroy the Supreme Intelligence which sparks the Kree Civil War.

watchFor.name: Maria Rambeau
watchFor.future: Carol's best friend, whose inclusion here is a setup for the broader multiverse as alternative versions of Maria appear later in the series.
watchFor.spoils: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness/The Marvels

watchFor.name: Monica Rambeau

watchFor.future: This movie sets up her growing up to get her own cosmic powers in WandaVision and fighting alongside Carol as an adult in The Marvels.

watchFor.name: Goose the Flerken

movies.title: Avengers: Endgame
movies.summary: With half of all life gone, the remaining Avengers assemble one final time to undo Thanos's actions.

beforeWatch.context: Picks up about 23 days after the Snap, with the survivors in pieces. It runs three hours and it leans on recognition harder than anything else in the run, so the more of the Infinity Saga you still have fresh, the more it hands back to you. Worth having straight going in, who is still standing: Tony and Nebula are stranded in space on Titan, and back on Earth it's Steve, Natasha, Thor, Bruce, Clint, Rhodey, Rocket and Okoye.

movies.timeSkip: Jumps forward 5 years partway through the film, from 2018 to 2023

deepDive.plot: Three weeks after the Snap, the surviving Avengers track down and kill Thanos, only to discover he's already destroyed the Infinity Stones. Five years later, Scott Lang's escape from the Quantum Realm reveals the possibility of time travel, and the remaining Avengers stage a 'time heist' across several past MCU films to collect past versions of the Stones and undo the Snap. Reversing the Snap brings back everyone who was dusted, but draws past Thanos into the present for one final battle, which Tony Stark wins at the cost of his own life.
deepDive.significance: Closes out the Infinity Saga, eleven years and twenty-two films. It reads like a grand ending, but it mostly sets up the characters and events the MCU spends the following phases building on. Every original Avenger either dies, retires or hands their job to someone else here, which is why so much of Phase Four is about people stepping into roles that used to belong to somebody more famous.
deepDive.orderNote: Sits at the end of Phase Three because it answers Infinity War directly. Captain Marvel goes in front of it rather than back in the 1990s where it actually takes place, so that the pager Fury sends at the end of Infinity War gets answered by someone you've already met.

watchFor.future: She's the Gamora in Vol. 3, and she doesn't remember Quill at all.

movies.title: WandaVision
movies.summary: Grieving in secret, Wanda Maximoff builds a sitcom life with a resurrected Vision in the town of Westview.

beforeWatch.context: Set about three weeks after the Blip, with some of the scenes outside Westview only a few days after it. Wanda lost her brother, her home and Vision across the last two Avengers films, and has had no time and nobody to process any of it with. The show opens as a black-and-white 1950s sitcom and stays in that format for several episodes. That is deliberate, not a mistake, and the decade it appears to be set in is never the decade it is actually set in.

deepDive.plot: Grieving Vision's death and unable to process her trauma from Thanos's Snap, Wanda Maximoff unknowingly seizes control of a small town, Westview, warping reality into a series of decades-spanning sitcom pastiches with a resurrected version of Vision built from her own grief and power. As S.W.O.R.D. investigates the anomaly from outside, the show reveals that Wanda's neighbor Agatha Harkness has secretly been manipulating events to steal Wanda's uniquely powerful magic. Wanda ultimately defeats Agatha, but has to say goodbye to the family she conjured, releasing the townspeople and leaving with the Darkhold to study her own powers in isolation.
deepDive.significance: The first Disney+ series, and the show that turns Wanda from an Avenger who has lost people into the Scarlet Witch. It introduces S.W.O.R.D., the off-world agency Monica's mother Maria Rambeau founded, and confirms the Skrulls are still operating on Earth. It also reopens where Wanda's powers came from: the films had them coming from the Mind Stone, and this show raises the possibility that the stone only amplified something she and Pietro already had, which is the closest the MCU has come to calling them mutants. White Vision and Agatha Harkness both start here and get picked up later.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed first in Phase Four as the earliest post-Endgame story, set only a few weeks after the Blip is reversed.

watchFor.name: Monica Rambeau
watchFor.thisFilm: The girl from Captain Marvel, grown up and working for S.W.O.R.D. She came back from the Blip to find her mother had died during the five years she missed.
watchFor.future: Passing through Wanda's barrier is what gives Monica her powers, and she is still working out how to use them in The Marvels.

watchFor.name: Darcy Lewis
watchFor.thisFilm: Jane Foster's intern from the Thor films, back with an actual doctorate and doing most of the useful thinking.

watchFor.name: Mrs. Hart
watchFor.future: Mrs. Hart turns up again in Agatha All Along.

watchFor.name: Agatha Harkness
watchFor.thisFilm: The nosy neighbour, and the one who has been prodding Wanda's grief all season to work out how she does what she does. Wanda beats her and then locks her inside the Agnes persona permanently.
watchFor.future: Agatha All Along opens with her still trapped in it.

watchFor.name: The Darkhold
watchFor.thisFilm: Agatha's book, which Wanda takes with her at the end and starts reading.
watchFor.future: The Darkhold is what Wanda is studying when Strange comes looking for her, and it is what turns her into the villain of that film.
watchFor.spoils: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness

watchFor.name: The post-credit scene
watchFor.thisFilm: A S.W.O.R.D. agent pulls Monica aside after everything is over. The agent is a Skrull, and she says someone off world wants to meet her.
watchFor.future: That meeting is what puts Monica in space for The Marvels.

watchFor.name: The twins
watchFor.thisFilm: Wanda has Billy and Tommy inside the Hex, and they go when it does.
watchFor.future: Hearing the twins call for her is what sends Wanda across the multiverse in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness. Billy comes back in Agatha All Along, reincarnated and looking for his brother.
watchFor.spoils: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness/Agatha All Along

watchFor.name: The second Vision
watchFor.thisFilm: S.W.O.R.D. rebuilds the real body, white and blank. The two Visions talk each other to a standstill instead of fighting, and the rebuilt one leaves with his memories back and no idea what to do with them.
watchFor.future: Nothing picks up the white Vision until VisionQuest.

episodes.title: Filmed Before a Live Studio Audience
episodes.summary: Wanda and Vision move into the town of Westview and settle into a black-and-white 1950s sitcom life, hiding what they can do from the neighbours, while a dinner with Vision's boss goes badly wrong.

watchFor.name: Mrs. Hart
watchFor.future: Mrs. Hart turns up again in Agatha All Along.

deepDive.plot: Wanda and Vision arrive in Westview as newlyweds in a black-and-white 1950s sitcom, with a heart drawn on the calendar and neither of them able to say what it marks. Vision hides that he is a synthezoid at work; Wanda uses her powers around the house whenever nobody is looking. The circled date turns out to be dinner with Vision's boss, Mr. Hart, and his wife, which Wanda has made no preparations for and improvises with magic. Mr. Hart begins choking at the table and Mrs. Hart keeps repeating at him to stop it, smiling, unable to do anything else. Wanda says stop it, and the moment resets as though it never happened. The episode ends with the whole thing revealed to be a broadcast that somebody is watching on a monitor.

episodes.title: Don't Touch That Dial
episodes.summary: The sitcom shifts into the 1960s as Wanda and Vision prepare for a magic show, while stranger anomalies creep into their perfect world.

deepDive.plot: The 1960s. Wanda and Vision rehearse a magic act for the neighbourhood talent show, with Agnes next door helping. A radio in the house cuts through the programme with a voice asking Wanda who is doing this to her. Vision accidentally swallows chewing gum and short-circuits, so the act has to be carried by real powers disguised as tricks. A beekeeper climbs out of a manhole in the street; Wanda says no and the episode rewinds itself. She is suddenly visibly pregnant, and as she and Vision stand outside, the world turns to colour.

episodes.title: Now in Color
episodes.summary: Now in the 1970s, Wanda's pregnancy accelerates unnaturally fast as the outside world starts to intrude on Westview.

deepDive.plot: The 1970s. Wanda's pregnancy runs from a bump to full term in a single afternoon, with Vision trying to arrange a doctor and the town behaving strangely around it. She gives birth to twins, Tommy and Billy. Their neighbour Geraldine is present, and when she mentions Ultron by name Wanda realises she is not part of the town at all. Wanda throws her out through the barrier, and outside, Geraldine lands in a field surrounded by military vehicles.

episodes.title: We Interrupt This Program
episodes.summary: Jumping outside Westview for the first time, S.W.O.R.D. investigates the strange sitcom-reality surrounding the town.

watchFor.name: Who Geraldine really is
watchFor.thisFilm: The neighbour who never quite fitted is Monica Rambeau, an agent who went into Westview from the outside and lost her own memory on the way in.

watchFor.name: The Rambeaus
watchFor.thisFilm: Monica is the girl from Captain Marvel, grown up. Her mother Maria was Carol Danvers' closest friend, and Monica returns from five years of the Blip to find that Maria died of cancer while she was gone.

watchFor.name: S.W.O.R.D.
watchFor.thisFilm: The agency running the perimeter, set up to handle threats from off-world. Maria Rambeau founded it.

watchFor.name: Seeing it from outside
watchFor.thisFilm: The episode restarts the series from the outside, and everything you have watched so far turns out to have been broadcast.

deepDive.plot: The series restarts from the outside.
