Monica Rambeau returns from the Blip in a hospital that is refilling with people, and learns her mother Maria died of cancer three years into the five she missed. She reports to S.W.O.R.D., the agency Maria founded, now run by Tyler Hayward. FBI agent Jimmy Woo has a missing persons case in Westview, a town nobody outside can remember exists, and astrophysicist Darcy Lewis picks up a broadcast signal coming out of it in the shape of a 1950s sitcom. Monica is sent in and comes out again after Wanda expels her. The episode replays that expulsion from Wanda's side, where Vision briefly appears as the corpse he actually is.

episodes.title: On a Very Special Episode...
episodes.summary: In an '80s-style episode, Wanda and Vision juggle twin toddlers while Vision starts to notice the townspeople aren't acting of their own free will.

watchFor.name: The twins
watchFor.thisFilm: Wanda's sons age themselves from babies to ten-year-olds in an afternoon and are named Billy and Tommy.

watchFor.name: What becomes of Billy
watchFor.future: Billy is the teenager at the centre of Agatha All Along, reincarnated and looking for his brother, and he takes the name Wiccan.

watchFor.name: Vision starts asking questions
watchFor.thisFilm: He works out that the townspeople are not choosing anything, and it is the first real argument he and Wanda have.

deepDive.plot: The 1980s. The twins age themselves to five and then to ten, and adopt a dog. Vision begins waking his colleagues out of Wanda's control at work and comes home to argue with her about whether any of this is a choice anyone is making. S.W.O.R.D. sends a drone in and Hayward fires on Wanda, who walks out of the Hex to tell them to leave her alone. Hayward shows the room security footage of Wanda stealing Vision's body from S.W.O.R.D., which is not what happened. The episode ends with someone knocking at the door: Wanda's brother Pietro, played by a different actor than the one who died in Sokovia.

episodes.title: All-New Halloween Spooktacular!
episodes.summary: A '90s-style Halloween episode as Vision investigates the truth about Westview just as a mysterious 'brother' of Pietro shows up.

deepDive.plot: A 1990s Halloween episode, with Pietro in the house and asking questions Wanda cannot answer. Billy and Tommy come into their powers, Billy hearing thoughts and Tommy running. Vision leaves the house and heads for the edge of town, finding the residents frozen mid-task the further out he goes, and begins tearing apart as he crosses the barrier. Darcy, inside the Hex and recruited into the sitcom as an escape artist, gets a message to him. To keep Vision alive Wanda expands the Hex outward, swallowing the S.W.O.R.D. camp and everyone in it.

episodes.title: Breaking the Fourth Wall
episodes.summary: The sitcom format collapses as Wanda begins to lose control of the reality she's created, revealing the toll of her grief.

watchFor.name: Agatha Harkness
watchFor.thisFilm: Revealed as the meddling neighbor who's been secretly manipulating events all along.
watchFor.future: Becomes the central antagonist of the finale, then gets her own spin-off.

deepDive.plot: A 2000s mockumentary, with Wanda talking to camera and her control slipping: objects change decade mid-shot and she cannot make them hold. Vision and Darcy make their way back into town. Monica forces her way through the barrier a second time and comes out the other side with her cells rewritten, seeing energy. Agnes takes the twins to her house. When Wanda follows, the basement is not a basement, and Agnes explains what she has been doing all season: she is Agatha Harkness, she has been there since the beginning, and none of it has been an accident.

episodes.title: Previously On
episodes.summary: Flashbacks reveal how Wanda's trauma and grief led her to unknowingly create the Hex and resurrect Vision using the Mind Stone's power.

watchFor.name: The Darkhold
watchFor.thisFilm: Wanda is shown the Darkhold, the 'Book of the Damned,' by Agatha.
watchFor.future: Becomes central to her descent into darkness in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness.
watchFor.spoils: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness

deepDive.plot: Agatha walks Wanda back through her own memories. A sitcom night in Sokovia interrupted by a Stark shell that killed her parents and then failed to go off for two days. The Hydra experiment with the Mind Stone, which did not give her power so much as find what was already there and make it enormous. Vision talking her through grief in the Avengers compound. Wanda going to S.W.O.R.D. to bury Vision and being refused, then walking to the plot of land in Westview he had bought for them, and creating everything out of nothing without meaning to. Agatha tells her what she is: the Scarlet Witch, a being that was supposed to be a myth. In the post-credits, Hayward brings the real Vision's body online, white and blank.

episodes.title: The Series Finale
episodes.summary: Wanda confronts Agatha for control of Westview and says goodbye to the family she created, while a mysterious white-caped figure appears in a mid-credit scene.

watchFor.name: White Vision
watchFor.thisFilm: A reconstructed, memory-wiped version of Vision built by S.W.O.R.D. confronts Wanda's Vision.
watchFor.future: Nothing picks up the white Vision until VisionQuest.

watchFor.name: Wanda reading the Darkhold
watchFor.thisFilm: Takes the Darkhold with her as she leaves Westview to study it in isolation.
watchFor.future: The Darkhold is what turns her into the villain of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness.
watchFor.spoils: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness

deepDive.plot: Wanda fights Agatha over Westview while Vision meets the rebuilt version of himself. The two Visions talk each other out of it instead of fighting, and the white one leaves with his memories restored and no idea what he is. Wanda lets Agatha drain her, having covered the Hex in runes so that only one witch can use magic inside it, and takes the Scarlet Witch title for herself. She traps Agatha inside the Agnes persona permanently. Then she takes the Hex down, which means saying goodbye to Vision and to the twins, and the townspeople look at her with no gratitude at all. In the mid-credits Monica is approached by a S.W.O.R.D. agent who is a Skrull, with a message that somebody off-world wants to meet her. In the post-credits Wanda is alone in a cabin in the mountains, astral-projecting over the Darkhold, and hears the twins calling for her.

movies.title: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier
movies.summary: With Steve Rogers gone, Sam Wilson and Bucky Barnes are forced to work together against a group of anti-nationalist super soldiers, while a new government-appointed Captain America stirs controversy.

beforeWatch.context: At the end of Endgame, Steve handed the shield to Sam Wilson. Sam has not decided what to do with it and is still serving, flying missions for the Air Force as Falcon. Bucky spent seventy years as a Hydra assassin with his memory wiped between jobs, chose to go back under in Wakanda after Civil War rather than risk being triggered again, and was deprogrammed there, which is where the Black Panther post-credits scene left him. Both of them are living in a world where half the population came back at once after five years away, and nobody has worked out what to do about the borders, the housing, or the people who filled the gap. The Winter Soldier is the film to have fresh.

movies.timeSkip: Roughly six months after the Blip is reversed

deepDive.plot: With Steve Rogers retired, Sam Wilson struggles with the weight of the shield he was given, ultimately donating it to a museum, while the government hands the Captain America mantle to a decorated but volatile soldier, John Walker. Sam and a restless Bucky Barnes reluctantly team up to stop the Flag-Smashers, a group of super-soldiers who believe the world was better during the Blip's more equal chaos. After Walker publicly kills a Flag-Smasher with the shield and is stripped of the title, Sam reclaims the mantle himself, becoming the first Black Captain America and confronting the government about America's history of failing Black soldiers like the forgotten super-soldier Isaiah Bradley.
deepDive.significance: The first thing the MCU made that is properly about the aftermath of the Blip rather than about a fight, which turns out to be the shape of most of Phase Four. It introduces Joaquin Torres and Isaiah Bradley, ends with Sam taking the name in a Wakandan-made suit, and turns John Walker into U.S. Agent working for Valentina. Sharon comes out of it pardoned and back inside the CIA, running something nobody in the series finds out about.
deepDive.orderNote: Follows WandaVision as the next chronological post-Blip story, unfolding over the following months.

watchFor.name: Sam Wilson
watchFor.thisFilm: Gives the shield up in the first episode because he does not think it is his to carry, and spends the series working out that he was wrong about why. He ends it as Captain America, in a suit Wakanda built for him, having taken the name on his own terms rather than the government's.
watchFor.future: He is Captain America from here, which is where Brave New World starts.

watchFor.name: Bucky Barnes
watchFor.thisFilm: Out of prison, in court-ordered therapy, working through a list of people he needs to make amends to. The list is the spine of his half of the series.
watchFor.future: He ends up in government himself years later, and on Valentina's team.

watchFor.name: Isaiah Bradley
watchFor.thisFilm: A super soldier from the Korean War who was used, imprisoned for thirty years, experimented on, and erased from the record by his own government.

watchFor.name: John Walker
watchFor.thisFilm: The government's replacement Captain America, who kills a surrendering man in a public square with the shield and is stripped of the title for it. Valentina recruits him before the episode is over and gives him a new suit and the name U.S. Agent.
watchFor.future: He is on the team in Thunderbolts*, still working for her.

watchFor.name: Valentina Allegra de Fontaine
watchFor.thisFilm: Turns up unannounced to recruit Walker, gives no straight answer about who she works for, and leaves.
watchFor.future: She has been assembling a team this whole time, which is what Thunderbolts* is.

watchFor.name: Sharon Carter
watchFor.thisFilm: Living in Madripoor since Civil War, abandoned by the people she helped. The last episode reveals she is the Power Broker, and she gets her pardon and her old CIA clearance back anyway.

episodes.title: New World Order
episodes.summary: Sam struggles with the weight of Steve's legacy while a new, more radical Captain America is unveiled by the government.

deepDive.plot: Sam flies an Air Force rescue over Tunisian airspace, pulling a hostage out of a hijacked transport while Georges Batroc's mercenaries try to stop him. Back home he hands the shield to the Smithsonian, saying it belongs in a museum rather than on a person. He and his sister Sarah are refused a bank loan on the family fishing boat despite Sam being an Avenger. Bucky is in court-ordered therapy, working through a list of people he wronged as the Winter Soldier, and is not telling Yori Nakajima that his son is on it. In Switzerland an organised group calling themselves the Flag-Smashers robs a bank with strength no ordinary person has. The episode ends with the government unveiling its own Captain America, holding the shield Sam gave away.

watchFor.name: Captain America
watchFor.thisFilm: Sam gives the shield up on the grounds that it belongs in a museum. The last shot of the episode is the government putting it on somebody else.

watchFor.name: Georges Batroc
watchFor.thisFilm: The mercenary from the opening of The Winter Soldier, back leading the hijacking Sam breaks up. He was captured in that film and is working again here.

episodes.title: The Star-Spangled Man
episodes.summary: Sam and Bucky reluctantly team up to track down the Flag-Smashers, a group fighting for a borderless world.

deepDive.plot: John Walker and his partner Lemar Hoskins do the press rounds, then turn up wanting Sam and Bucky's help. Sam and Bucky ambush a Flag-Smasher convoy in Munich and are comprehensively beaten: every one of them is a super soldier. Walker and Hoskins arrive and it still goes badly. Bucky takes Sam to Baltimore to meet Isaiah Bradley, a super soldier from the Korean War who fought the Winter Soldier in 1951, and who was imprisoned and experimented on for thirty years afterwards while his records were erased. Bucky is arrested for skipping therapy and Walker gets him out. Out of options, they decide to go and see the one man who understands super soldiers better than anyone.

episodes.title: Power Broker
episodes.summary: The hunt for the source of the Flag-Smashers' powers leads Sam and Bucky to enlist the unpredictable Baron Zemo.

deepDive.plot: Bucky breaks Helmut Zemo out of a Berlin prison. The three go to Madripoor, where Sam has to impersonate the crime lord Smiling Tiger and Bucky has to pretend to still be the Winter Soldier. They find Sharon Carter, living there as a fugitive, and through her the scientist Wilfred Nagel, who recreated the super soldier serum for the Power Broker and produced twenty vials that Karli Morgenthau stole. Zemo kills Nagel. Karli bombs a Global Repatriation Council facility. The episode ends in Latvia with Ayo of the Dora Milaje telling Bucky she has come for Zemo.

watchFor.name: Helmut Zemo
watchFor.thisFilm: The Sokovian colonel from Civil War, who lost his wife, son and father when Ultron dropped their city, and who worked out that the Avengers could be broken from the inside rather than beaten. He was serving a life sentence in Berlin for it. He is not enhanced, he is not strong, and he is one of the most dangerous in the series.

watchFor.name: Sharon Carter
watchFor.thisFilm: Peggy Carter's great-niece, the S.H.I.E.L.D. agent who stole the shield and the wings back for Steve and Sam during Civil War. That made her a criminal under the Sokovia Accords, and unlike them she had no Wakanda to disappear into and nobody lobbying for a pardon. She has been on the run in Madripoor ever since, and she is not warm about it.

episodes.title: The Whole World is Watching
episodes.summary: Tensions boil over as John Walker's actions as the new Captain America spiral out of control.

deepDive.plot: A flashback shows Ayo deprogramming Bucky in Wakanda, breaking Hydra's trigger words for good. In the present the Dora Milaje come to take Zemo, and Walker tries to pull rank on them and is put on the floor. Sam gets a conversation with Karli that is close to working before Walker interrupts it. Zemo destroys the remaining serum vials, but Walker has already pocketed one and takes it. Karli kills Lemar Hoskins in the fight that follows. Walker chases one of the Flag-Smashers into a public square and beats him to death with the shield in front of a crowd of phones.

watchFor.name: The Dora Milaje
watchFor.thisFilm: Wakanda's royal guard, introduced in Black Panther as the king's personal protection and the country's standing army. Ayo leads the detail that spent years undoing what Hydra did to Bucky's head, which is why they have a claim on Zemo and why Bucky will not fight them.

episodes.title: Truth
episodes.summary: Sam confronts the government and Isaiah Bradley, a forgotten Black super-soldier erased from history, about who gets to be a hero.

deepDive.plot: Sam and Bucky take the shield off Walker by force. Walker is stripped of rank and of the title in a hearing, and is approached immediately afterwards by a woman who declines to explain who she works for. Sam goes back to Baltimore and Isaiah tells him the whole of it: sent to destroy the Winter Soldier, imprisoned for thirty years, experimented on by his own government, his existence deleted from the record. Sam takes the shield home to Louisiana, works on the boat with Sarah, and starts training with it. Bucky arrives with a case from Wakanda. Zemo is taken to the Raft by the Dora Milaje.

episodes.title: One World, One People
episodes.summary: Sam claims the mantle of Captain America for the first time, addressing the world directly about what the shield should stand for.

watchFor.name: Sam Wilson becomes Captain America
watchFor.thisFilm: Takes up the shield and the name, in a suit Wakanda built for him, and does it on his own terms rather than the government's.
watchFor.future: He is Captain America from here, which is where Brave New World starts.

watchFor.name: Isaiah Bradley's memorial
watchFor.thisFilm: Sam gets an exhibit put into the Smithsonian for him. Isaiah spends the scene not believing anyone would do it. He stops being a man the country erased and becomes a man it has to admit to.
watchFor.future: That public existence is what makes him matter again in Brave New World.

watchFor.name: Sharon back inside the CIA
watchFor.thisFilm: Pardoned, reinstated, and on the phone within the hour arranging to sell government secrets and prototypes. Nobody in the series finds out.

deepDive.plot: Sam arrives at the Global Repatriation Council vote in a Wakandan-made suit as Captain America. The Flag-Smashers' attack is stopped, Sharon shoots Karli, and Sam refuses to let the moment end there: he makes the GRC listen to why people were desperate enough to follow her. Walker helps rather than pursues. Afterwards Sharon is pardoned and reinstated at the CIA, and the last thing she does is make a call proving she is still the Power Broker, now with clearance. Valentina hands Walker a new suit and a new name. Sam takes Isaiah and his grandson Eli to the Smithsonian, where an exhibit has been added for a super soldier nobody was allowed to know about.

movies.title: Spider-Man: Far From Home
movies.summary: While on a school trip across Europe, Peter Parker is recruited by Nick Fury to help a mysterious visitor from another dimension battle a string of elemental creatures threatening the world.

beforeWatch.context: Tony Stark is dead. He used the Stones himself at the end of Endgame and it killed him, and Peter has not worked out what to do with that. This is eight months after the Blip put everyone back, and the five missing years only happened to the people who stayed. An older sibling who was dusted can come back younger than the younger one who was not. Peter's whole year group returned at the age they left and walked into a school that had carried on for five years without them. He is going to Europe on a school trip and would like a holiday.

movies.timeSkip: Eight months after the Blip brought everyone back

deepDive.plot: Grieving Tony Stark and dodging every call from Nick Fury, Peter Parker leaves for a school trip to Europe wanting two weeks off. Fury takes the trip over anyway and pairs him with Quentin Beck, a hero calling himself Mysterio who says he is from another Earth and is hunting the elemental creatures that destroyed it. Beck is lying. He is a former Stark employee running a drone army and a projection rig built out of Stark tech, staging every attack so he can beat it on camera and inherit Tony's place. Peter hands him EDITH, Tony's defence system, before he works any of it out, then takes it back off him over London. Beck dies under his own drones, and the footage his team puts out afterwards names Peter Parker as Spider-Man.
deepDive.significance: One of the first titles, alongside The Falcon and the Winter Soldier, to deal with the state the Blip left the world in. Beck's cover story is the first time an MCU film puts numbers on separate Earths. He names his as Earth-833, and he names this one as Earth-616. The Skrulls are still standing in for Fury eight months after Endgame. And it ends by taking Peter's mask off in front of the whole world, which is the premise the next film runs on.
deepDive.orderNote: Set in the summer of 2024, about two months after The Falcon and the Winter Soldier. No Way Home sits immediately after it because it picks up in the moment the mid-credits scene ends.

watchFor.name: How the world talks about the Blip
EDITH
watchFor.thisFilm: Tony leaves Peter a pair of glasses wired into Stark defence systems, including an orbital drone array, and Peter is sixteen.

watchFor.name: Quentin Beck
watchFor.thisFilm: Presents himself as a hero from another Earth. He's a former Stark employee with a grudge and a very good illusion rig, and the whole crisis is staged.

watchFor.name: The multiverse pitch
watchFor.future: The lie is not far off. Beck calls his home world Earth-833 and this one Earth-616, and No Way Home makes other Earths real by pulling people out of them. Loki puts the whole branching structure on screen not long after.

watchFor.name: Happy Hogan
watchFor.thisFilm: Last seen at Tony's funeral in Endgame. Here he flies the class around Europe, runs errands for Fury, and is seeing May Parker, which Peter finds out by walking in on the pair of them.

watchFor.name: MJ and Ned
watchFor.thisFilm: MJ works out who he is on her own, from watching him, before he ever tells her. Ned spends the trip attached to Betty Brant.

watchFor.name: J. Jonah Jameson
watchFor.thisFilm: The mid-credits hands Beck's doctored footage to a bellowing tabloid broadcaster, and it is J.K. Simmons in the chair, twenty years after he played the part in the Raimi films.

watchFor.name: Nick Fury & Maria Hill (post-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: The Fury and Hill running Peter all film are Talos and Soren wearing their faces, last seen as themselves in Captain Marvel in 1995. The real Fury is off-world on a Skrull ship, which is where WandaVision's post-credit scene already put him when a Skrull came to fetch Monica Rambeau on his behalf.
watchFor.future: Fury stays up there. The Marvels finds him running a station in orbit, and Secret Invasion is about what the Skrulls on Earth have been doing while he was gone.

movies.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
movies.summary: After his identity is exposed, Peter Parker asks Doctor Strange for help, and a spell gone wrong tears open the multiverse, bringing dangerous visitors from other realities into his world.

beforeWatch.context: Spider-Man: No Way Home starts right where Spider-Man: Far From Home left off. Beck's fake video exposed Peter Parker as Spider-Man and frames him for murder and the drone strike in London. The other thing to know is that this story has countless references from the five previous Spider-Man films released between 2002 and 2014. Those movies are listed under 'Helps, but optional' below. If you haven't seen those movies it would be a big mistake to continue, so I would highly recommend going back to watch or even rewatch them first.

movies.timeSkip: Picks up in the moment Far From Home ends

deepDive.plot: With his identity publicly exposed and his loved ones' lives upended, Peter Parker asks Doctor Strange to cast a spell making the world forget he's Spider-Man, but Peter's own hesitations corrupt the spell, tearing open the multiverse and pulling in villains, and eventually the Spider-Men themselves, from other Spider-Man universes entirely. After a version of Peter's Aunt May is killed trying to save one of the villains, Peter chooses to help redeem all of them rather than send them back to certain death, at the cost of having Strange erase the entire world's memory of him, which leaves Peter with nothing and no one who knows him.
deepDive.significance: Two alternate versions of Earth bleed into this reality, bringing along two older versions of Peter Parker. In a tragic twist, Aunt May is the one who delivers the famous line about power and responsibility right before she dies, whereas Uncle Ben said it in the other two universes. The Department of Damage Control, the agency created to clean up after the Chitauri came through New York in 2012 and last seen in Spider-Man: Homecoming, is the group building the legal case against Peter. To fight these charges, Peter hires defense attorney Matt Murdock, a cameo that officially brings Charlie Cox's Daredevil into the main movie timeline. Ultimately, the film ends with a massive spell that forces every single person alive to completely forget that Peter Parker exists, which sets the stage for the next Spider-Man movie.
deepDive.orderNote: Starts in the summer of 2024, in the moment Far From Home's mid-credits scene ends, and runs through to Christmas. Following right after these events, the Disney+ series Hawkeye takes place over that very same New York City Christmas season.

watchFor.name: The Department of Damage Control
watchFor.thisFilm: This federal organization, which handles cleaning up after superhero battles ever since the alien Chitauri invaded New York in 2012, was first introduced in Spider-Man: Homecoming as the group in charge of the city's salvage contract. The agents raid Peter's apartment and take Peter, MJ, Ned, and Aunt May into custody for questioning.
watchFor.future: The Department of Damage Control is a recurring agency that shows up in the series She-Hulk, Ms. Marvel and Wonder Man, and in the film Spider-Man: Brand New Day.
watchFor.spoils: She-Hulk: Attorney at Law/Ms. Marvel/Spider-Man: Brand New Day

watchFor.name: Peter's lawyer
watchFor.future: Matt Murdock, played by Charlie Cox, makes his first official appearance in the main movie timeline. This cameo serves as a massive milestone for fans because it officially brings the entire Netflix series directly into main MCU canon. He shows up in She-Hulk and Echo after this, and later gets his own series in Daredevil: Born Again.

watchFor.name: Multiversal visitors
watchFor.future: First hard proof the multiverse is real to people on Earth, and Strange spends his next film dealing with the consequences.
watchFor.spoils: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness

watchFor.name: May Parker
watchFor.thisFilm: Dies at Osborn's hands, and says the line about power and responsibility to Peter just before she does. In the other two universes that was Ben.

watchFor.name: The other two
watchFor.thisFilm: Peter 2 and Peter 3, acting as older mentors who use their own past tragedies to teach Peter 1 important life lessons. By learning from his variants, Peter 1 gains a deeper maturity that will shape his choices in all future movies.

watchFor.name: MJ and Ned
watchFor.thisFilm: Both of them get into MIT. Peter does not, and the last look at his new flat has a GED study guide sitting on the desk.

watchFor.name: What the last spell costs
watchFor.thisFilm: Strange erases Peter Parker from everyone's memory to close the multiverse. Not just his identity. Him. Spider-Man is still public knowledge, the mask and the name and everything he has done, and it is Peter Parker nobody can remember. MJ and Ned don't know he exists, and he chooses not to tell them.
watchFor.future: He ends the film broke, alone, in a bedsit, sewing his own suit with no Stark tech and no Avengers connections. Brand New Day starts from there.

watchFor.name: Eddie Brock (post-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: Blips out of the bar mid-sentence and leaves a piece of the symbiote behind on the counter. Nothing has picked it up yet, and it is the one loose thread that could put this Peter in a symbiote suit later.

movies.title: Hawkeye
movies.summary: Clint Barton teams up with young archer Kate Bishop to take down a criminal conspiracy tied to his past as Ronin, just days before Christmas.

beforeWatch.context: Clint Barton lost his entire family to Thanos's snap. He spent the five years of the Blip as Ronin, a masked vigilante who worked through criminal organisations around the world and killed almost everyone he found, and that is the past this series is built on. Going in, the Avengers no longer exist as a team and Avengers Tower has been sold. This is set a few days after Spider-Man: No Way Home, so there are background details of the damage that film did to New York scattered through it. There are also references to the Netflix series Daredevil. Those matter far less here than the older Spider-Man films did to No Way Home, and skipping them costs you very little.

deepDive.plot: Trying to get home to his family for Christmas, retired Avenger Clint Barton is dragged back into his past as the vigilante Ronin when aspiring young archer Kate Bishop accidentally puts on his old suit at an auction, drawing the attention of a tracksuit-wearing mafia and Yelena Belova, who blames Clint for Natasha's death. Clint and Kate team up, uncovering that the real villain is a mob boss connected to Kate's own family, and Clint clears his name with Yelena while passing his archer's mantle informally to Kate.
deepDive.significance: Introduces Maya Lopez, who goes on to get her own series. It also brings back Vincent D'Onofrio as Wilson Fisk, playing Maya's uncle, which makes him the second major character to cross over from the Netflix Daredevil series after Matt Murdock did it a few days earlier in No Way Home. Most of the series is Clint settling his own accounts. He convinces Yelena Belova that Natasha chose to sacrifice herself rather than being killed for it, which ends Yelena's grudge against him, and he tells Maya that her father was given up by Fisk rather than singled out by Ronin. By the end Clint trusts Kate Bishop completely and gives her the name, which makes her the second Hawkeye.
deepDive.orderNote: Set at Christmas 2024, a few days after Spider-Man: No Way Home, and placed directly after it.

watchFor.name: Clint just wants to get home for Christmas
Kate Bishop
watchFor.thisFilm: Twenty-two, extremely good, and completely unprepared for what the job actually involves. She saw Clint fight in New York as a child and has been aiming at this ever since.
watchFor.future: Ends the series with the name, and she's one of the Young Avengers the MCU keeps quietly assembling. She turns up again at the end of The Marvels, where Ms. Marvel comes to recruit her for a team she is putting together.

watchFor.name: Jack Duquesne
watchFor.thisFilm: Eleanor Bishop's fiancé, a master fencer with a collection of swords, and the man the series spends five episodes pointing at. Kate is certain he is behind all of it. What he actually turns out to be is the CEO of Sloan Limited, the company laundering money for the Tracksuit Mafia, and he is arrested for that at the end.
watchFor.future: He comes back years later in Daredevil: Born Again as the vigilante Swordsman.

watchFor.name: Maya Lopez
watchFor.thisFilm: Deaf, reading lips, running the Tracksuit Mafia and after Ronin for killing her father. Her uncle turns out to be the man who gave him up.
watchFor.future: Walks away from all of it, which is where Echo starts. That series sends her home to Oklahoma and is about her unlocking the abilities she inherited from her ancestors.

watchFor.name: Yelena Belova
watchFor.thisFilm: Turns up hunting Clint because Valentina told her he killed Natasha. The rooftop conversation where she finds out otherwise is the best scene in the show.
watchFor.future: She's on Valentina's team by Thunderbolts*, still carrying this.

watchFor.name: Kingpin
watchFor.thisFilm: Maya's uncle and the man behind the Tracksuits, brought back for the first time since the Netflix run. Maya shoots him at the end and the series leaves him presumed dead.
watchFor.future: He survived. Echo picks him up again, and in Daredevil: Born Again he is elected mayor of New York.

postCredit.skipNote: Black Widow's credit scene told you to skip it and come back right before Hawkeye. This is that point, so go and watch it now.

episodes.title: Never Meet Your Heroes
episodes.summary: Kate Bishop accidentally puts on a mysterious Ronin suit at an auction, drawing Clint Barton back into a world he'd hoped to leave behind.

deepDive.plot: The episode opens in 2012, during the Battle of New York. A young Kate Bishop watches from her bedroom window as Clint Barton fires arrows from a rooftop, and her father is killed when the building is hit. Kate tells her mother Eleanor she wants to learn to protect the family, and takes up archery. Twelve years later Kate is sent home from college after destroying a bell tower with an arrow to win a bet. Back in New York she meets Eleanor's fiancé Jack Duquesne, who beats her in a fencing match, and she takes an immediate dislike to him. Meanwhile Clint is in the city with his children for Christmas, sitting through Rogers: The Musical and its version of the Battle of New York. Kate follows Jack to a black-market auction at a private club, where the Ronin suit is up for sale along with the sword Jack later takes home. The Tracksuit Mafia raids the auction, and Kate puts the suit on to fight her way out. She is filmed doing it. Clint sees the footage on the news, realises someone is walking around New York dressed as Ronin, and goes to find her.

episodes.title: Hide and Seek
episodes.summary: Clint and Kate try to track down the tracksuit-wearing gang hunting the Ronin suit before Christmas gets any more complicated.

deepDive.plot: Clint takes the Ronin suit off Kate and tells her to stay out of it, then puts his children on a train home. The Tracksuit Mafia work out who Kate is and firebomb her apartment, so Clint reluctantly moves her to her aunt's place. Kate discovers that Armand Duquesne, Jack's uncle, has been murdered, and that the sword Jack bought at the auction matches the wound, which convinces her Jack is a killer. Clint tracks his stolen equipment to a LARP tournament in a park and retrieves the Ronin suit from a firefighter named Grills by fighting his way through the event. He also records a video explaining Ronin, meaning to give himself up. The Tracksuits catch Clint and Kate at the end of the episode, and when Clint asks who is really in charge, he is taken to meet Maya Lopez.

episodes.title: Echoes
episodes.summary: The pair run into Maya Lopez, a deaf crime-family enforcer with her own grudge against Ronin.

deepDive.plot: The episode opens on Maya Lopez's childhood. Deaf and sent to a hearing school, she learns to read people and to fight, taught by her father William, who runs the Tracksuit Mafia, and encouraged by her uncle. Her father is killed by Ronin during the Blip, and Maya has been hunting him since. In the present she interrogates Clint, who escapes with Kate. The two of them get out through a car chase across Brooklyn in which Clint runs through his trick arrows, including a Pym Particle arrow that turns a car enormous. Clint explains to Kate that Ronin was him, and that he did what he did during the five years he lost his family. He tells her the people hunting the suit will not stop, and orders her to go home. Maya, meanwhile, is warned by her second-in-command Kazi that she is pushing too hard, and she works out that Ronin and Hawkeye are the same man.

episodes.title: Partners, Am I Right?
episodes.summary: Clint and Kate go after a stolen watch that could expose a former S.H.I.E.L.D. agent, and the job goes wrong on a rooftop.

deepDive.plot: Clint and Kate go after the Rolex recovered from the auction, which belongs to a former S.H.I.E.L.D. agent whose identity would be exposed if the Tracksuits kept it. Eleanor meets Clint privately and tells him to keep her daughter out of it. Kate brings Clint to her mother's Christmas party, where Clint borrows a suit and Kate needles Jack. The pair break into Maya's apartment to steal the watch and are caught, and the fight spills onto the rooftop. Maya fights Clint, and a second masked figure arrives and goes after Kate. Clint burns the Ronin suit, deciding he is finished with it. On the roof Kate pulls the mask off her attacker, and it is Yelena Belova.

episodes.title: Ronin
episodes.summary: Clint faces up to the Ronin years, and Kate gets an unexpected visitor.

deepDive.plot: A flashback shows Yelena Belova returning from the Blip in Ohio, five years after she vanished, and being told that Natasha is dead. Valentina Allegra de Fontaine hires her and names Clint Barton as the man responsible. In the present Yelena lets herself into Kate's apartment, and the two of them eat macaroni cheese while Yelena explains, cheerfully, that she has been contracted to kill Clint. Kate realises the contract came from her own mother. Clint finally calls Maya and tells her the truth about her father: Ronin was given his location by someone inside her own organisation, and that someone was her uncle. Kate finds proof that Eleanor has been working for Fisk, and shows Clint. The episode ends with Clint naming the man behind everything, and Wilson Fisk appears on screen.

episodes.title: So This Is Christmas?
episodes.summary: Clint and Kate team up to take down the head of the criminal conspiracy once and for all, on Christmas Eve.

deepDive.plot: On Christmas Eve, Eleanor meets Fisk to tell him she is finished, and he makes it clear she is not. Clint and Kate set a trap at the Rockefeller Center holiday party, arming themselves with trick arrows and pulling in the LARPers as backup. The Tracksuits attack. Clint fights and kills Kazi, Kate works through the rest with her arrows, and Yelena finds Clint on the roof. He tells her that Natasha chose to die to save everyone and was not murdered for it, and proves he is telling the truth with the whistle Natasha taught them both. Yelena hits him once and leaves. Kate confronts Fisk in the street and takes him apart with the last of her trick arrows. Maya finds him in the alley afterwards and shoots him. Eleanor is arrested for Armand's murder, and Jack Duquesne is arrested over Sloan Limited. Clint brings Kate back to the farm for Christmas, they burn the Ronin suit together, and he gives her the name.

movies.title: Echo
movies.summary: Maya Lopez goes back to the Choctaw town in Oklahoma she grew up in, and finds that neither her family nor the life she left in New York is willing to let her start over quietly.

beforeWatch.context: This carries straight on from Hawkeye, about five months later. What you need from that series is Maya. Her father ran the Tracksuit Mafia and was killed on Ronin's blade, she grew up around Wilson Fisk, who she called her uncle and who was closer to her than her own family was, and the last thing she did in that show was find out he had arranged her father's death and she shoots Fisk in the head for it. She left New York the same night. It is five episodes, much smaller than most series, and most of it takes place in one small Oklahoma town.

deepDive.plot: Maya Lopez grew up in Tamaha, Oklahoma. Her mother was killed in a car crash when Maya was a child, her father took her to New York afterwards, and Wilson Fisk took an interest in her there and raised her into an enforcer. At the end of Hawkeye she found out Fisk had arranged her father's killing, and she shot him for it. This picks up five months later, with Maya back in Tamaha for the first time in years, in a town and a family that did not ask her to come home. She wants to take Fisk's operation apart from a distance and leans on relatives who want nothing to do with any of it. Then she starts seeing things she cannot explain: her own Choctaw ancestors, a line of women reaching back to the first of them, each carrying something she is meant to inherit. Fisk is not dead. He sends people to Tamaha, and when that fails he comes himself. It ends at a Choctaw Nation powwow with her family in the middle of it, where Maya finally takes hold of what her ancestors left her and turns it on Fisk, putting his own childhood back in front of him. He leaves Tamaha, and he leaves her alone.
deepDive.significance: Deals with the aftermath of Maya's break with Wilson Fisk, and explains where her abilities actually come from, which is a Choctaw lineage rather than anything the MCU had set up before. It is also the first MCU series built around a deaf, Indigenous lead, and the sound design works accordingly. Beyond that it is self-contained. It leads directly into Daredevil: Born Again and does very little else for the wider MCU, so of everything in this phase it is the one you can skip without missing much.
deepDive.orderNote: Placed directly after Hawkeye, five months on, as the straight continuation of Maya's story from that series.

watchFor.name: How the series uses sound
watchFor.thisFilm: Maya is deaf, and the show puts you in that position rather than describing it. Sound drops out, comes back through vibration and floorboards, and a good deal of the dialogue is signed. Worth watching somewhere quiet.

watchFor.name: The episode titles
watchFor.thisFilm: Each of the five is named for one of Maya's Choctaw ancestors, and each opens on that ancestor's story before returning to the present. The last one is named for Maya.

watchFor.name: Maya's family in Tamaha
watchFor.thisFilm: She left this town years ago and did not part well with anyone in it. The relatives she comes back to are not pleased to see her and are not written as obstacles either, which is most of what the series is actually about.

watchFor.name: Kingpin
watchFor.thisFilm: He survived being shot. He comes to Tamaha in person to get Maya back, and what stops him is not a fight. Maya reaches him through the same ancestral connection she has spent the series learning, and makes him look at his own childhood. He leaves without her.
watchFor.future: Daredevil: Born Again picks him up from here, where he has turned respectable and is running for mayor of New York.

episodes.title: Chafa
episodes.summary: Maya's life before Tamaha, and the night she decided she was finished with New York.

deepDive.plot: The episode opens on Chafa, the first of Maya's ancestors, and the origin the Choctaw tell about her. Then Tamaha, Oklahoma, and Maya as a child, until her mother is killed in a car crash and her father takes her to New York. Wilson Fisk takes an interest in her there, and over the years he raises her into something useful to him, closer to her than her own family ever managed. In the present she learns that her father's killing was arranged by Fisk himself. She shoots him for it and leaves the city that night.

episodes.title: Lowak
episodes.summary: Back in Tamaha, Maya starts working on Fisk's operation from a distance and gets nowhere with her family.

deepDive.plot: Maya arrives back in Tamaha for the first time in years and sets herself up at her uncle's skating rink. Her plan is to take Fisk's operation apart from out here, and it needs people, so she goes to the family she walked out on. They are not interested, and they are not shy about why. Between the arguments she starts seeing things she cannot account for, images of people she has never met that arrive without warning.

episodes.title: Tuklo
episodes.summary: Fisk's people arrive in town, and Maya finds out what she has brought with her.

deepDive.plot: Fisk's crew reach Tamaha. Whatever Maya thought she was doing at a safe distance is now happening on the street where her relatives live and work, and other people start paying for it. The episode sets her history against theirs: what she learned in New York works, and it costs the town something every time she uses it.

episodes.title: Taloa
episodes.summary: Maya is caught between the life Fisk built for her and the one she left behind.

deepDive.plot: Maya reaches the point where she has to choose which of the two things she is going to be. The visions have stopped being random and started being an inheritance, one that only works if she is willing to be part of a line rather than the last one standing. Her family has its own history with all of this, and most of that history is about people who did not get the chance.

episodes.title: Maya
episodes.summary: Everything comes to a head at the Choctaw Nation powwow.

deepDive.plot: Fisk's people hit the Choctaw Nation powwow with Maya's family in the middle of it. Maya finally takes hold of what her ancestors have been offering her all season, and it turns out not to be a weapon in the way she expected. Fisk comes for her himself, and she reaches him through the same connection, putting his own childhood in front of him until he cannot look away from it. He leaves. Maya stays, and the family she came back to is still standing.

movies.title: Loki: Season 1
movies.summary: After stealing the Tesseract during the Avengers' 2012 time heist, a variant of the God of Mischief is arrested by the Time Variance Authority.

beforeWatch.context: Loki was killed by Thanos in the opening scene of Avengers: Infinity War, and that has not been undone. He is still dead. This series is not about him. It follows the 2012 version of Loki from The Avengers, the one who grabbed the Tesseract and vanished during the time heist in Endgame. While you watch, pay close attention to what the TVA is for and to the rules they lay out for the Sacred Timeline. Both of those matter a great deal to the phases that follow.

deepDive.plot: The 2012 Loki escapes with the Tesseract during the Avengers' time heist and lands in the Gobi Desert, where the Time Variance Authority arrest him for stepping off the Sacred Timeline. He is told he can be erased or he can help, and an analyst named Mobius puts him to work hunting a variant of himself who has been ambushing TVA units and stealing their reset charges. The variant is Sylvie, a Loki taken by the TVA as a child. The two of them end up stranded together on Lamentis-1 as the moon is destroyed, and the connection that forms between them creates a branch large enough to bring the TVA down on both of them. They break into the Time-Keepers' chamber and find that the three rulers of the organisation are mindless androids, which means nobody at the TVA knows who is actually in charge. Loki is pruned and wakes in the Void, a wasteland at the end of time where everything the TVA deletes is dumped, patrolled by a creature called Alioth. With help from other exiled Loki variants he and Sylvie get past Alioth and reach the citadel beyond it, where they meet He Who Remains, the man who built the TVA. He offers them his job and tells them what happens if they turn it down. Sylvie kills him anyway. The Sacred Timeline splits into countless branches, and Loki is thrown back into a TVA where nobody recognises him and the statues are of Kang.
deepDive.significance: Introduces the idea that there is more than one timeline. It also answers the question Endgame left hanging, which is what became of the 2012 Loki who disappeared with the Tesseract. It introduces He Who Remains, a thirty-first century variant of the man who becomes Kang the Conqueror, and it introduces the Void and Alioth. From here the MCU is a setting with infinite possibilities rather than one fixed history. This is also a good point to pick up What If...?, which is not required for anything but runs on exactly that idea.
deepDive.orderNote: This one could sit in several places. The Loki it follows is taken from The Avengers in 2012, and the moment he escapes belongs to the time heist in Endgame, so either of those could work. Putting it at the very start of Phase Four would cut across the post-Blip stories, and putting it at the end would leave the Multiverse Saga with no introduction. Watch it before Quantumania, because that film's villain only lands once you've met He Who Remains.

watchFor.name: The TVA
watchFor.thisFilm: An organisation outside time that prunes any timeline branching off the approved one, staffed by people who believe they were created for the job. They weren't. They're all variants themselves, taken from their own lives and mind-wiped.
watchFor.future: In Season 2 and the phases after it the TVA carry on managing the multiverse rather than pruning it, and Loki ends up as the God of Stories holding the branches together.

watchFor.name: The rules of the timeline
watchFor.thisFilm: The series stops to explain how all of this works, and it is worth following closely. One approved history, called the Sacred Timeline. Anything that deviates from it is a nexus event, which grows into a branch. The TVA prune the branch with a reset charge and arrest whoever caused it, and that person is a variant. Every multiverse story after this one runs on these terms.

watchFor.name: Which Loki this is
watchFor.thisFilm: The 2012 version who grabbed the Tesseract during the Endgame heist. He hasn't had Thor: The Dark World or Ragnarok.

watchFor.name: Mobius
watchFor.thisFilm: The analyst assigned to him, and the first person to treat Loki as someone worth arguing with rather than containing.

watchFor.name: Sylvie
watchFor.thisFilm: A Loki variant taken by the TVA as a child, who has spent her whole life since trying to burn it down. She's the season's other half, not a love interest bolted on.

watchFor.name: The man at the end of time
watchFor.thisFilm: The citadel at the end of the season holds a tired man who set the TVA up to stop his own variants from finding each other. He is a thirty-first century scientist who found the other timelines first, fought a war against his own variants and won it, and pruned everything else to keep them from ever meeting again. He offers Loki and Sylvie the job, tells them what happens if they refuse, and Sylvie kills him anyway.
watchFor.future: Quantumania introduces one of the variants he was afraid of, and season two is entirely about whether he was telling the truth.
watchFor.spoils: Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania/Loki: Season 2

watchFor.name: The Void and Alioth
watchFor.thisFilm: The Void is the end of time, where everything the TVA prunes is sent rather than destroyed. Alioth is the living storm that grazes on it, and the reason nothing the TVA deletes ever comes back.
watchFor.future: Both turn up again in Deadpool & Wolverine, which is largely set in the Void.

watchFor.name: The multiverse unleashed
watchFor.thisFilm: Sylvie's choice at the citadel is the moment the Sacred Timeline stops being single. It branches, and keeps branching, and nothing after this happens in a universe with only one possible history.

episodes.title: Glorious Purpose
episodes.summary: A 2012 variant of Loki is arrested by the TVA the moment he escapes with the Tesseract, and given an impossible choice to avoid being erased from existence.

deepDive.plot: Loki escapes the Avengers with the Tesseract in 2012 and lands in the Gobi Desert, where a squad of TVA Minutemen led by Hunter B-15 arrest him within seconds. He is processed through an office that treats a god as paperwork, told that the Time Variance Authority exists to protect the Sacred Timeline, and put in front of Judge Ravonna Renslayer, who sentences him to be reset. An analyst named Mobius pulls him out of the queue instead. Mobius shows him his own file, including the deaths further along the timeline he was taken from, and Loki watches Frigga die and then watches Thanos kill him. It breaks the performance. Mobius explains that he wants Loki's help catching a variant who has been killing TVA units, and reveals the fugitive is another Loki.

episodes.title: The Variant
episodes.summary: Loki is recruited to help TVA agent Mobius hunt a mysterious variant who's been killing Minutemen across the timeline.

deepDive.plot: Loki is put to work in the TVA archives while Mobius tries to work out where the variant will strike next. Loki reads TVA doctrine, learns about the Time-Keepers, and notices that a Loki hiding somewhere would pick a disaster large enough to cover any damage he caused. That leads them to a hurricane in Alabama in 2050, where the variant has been hiding inside the storm and stockpiling reset charges. B-15 is enchanted and used as a mouthpiece. The variant turns out to be a woman, and when she has the charges she sends them all through the doors at once. Every timeline she has seeded branches at the same moment, and the Sacred Timeline lights up. She escapes through a portal, and Loki follows her.

episodes.title: Lamentis
episodes.summary: Loki and the variant Sylvie are stranded together on a moon about to be destroyed, forcing an uneasy alliance.

deepDive.plot: Loki and the other variant land on Lamentis-1, a mining moon in 2077 that is about to be destroyed by its own planet falling on it. Her TemPad is out of power, so they have to reach an evacuation ark before the moon breaks apart, which means a long walk and a train ride. She tells him her name is Sylvie and that the TVA took her as a child, that she has been running ever since, and that she does not know anything about her own past. Loki tells her the TVA agents are not created by the Time-Keepers, and she tells him they are: they are all variants who have been mind-wiped. Loki gets drunk on the train and gets them both thrown off, destroying the TemPad in the fall. They reach the ark just in time to watch it be destroyed, and the episode ends with the two of them stranded on a moon with hours left.

episodes.title: The Nexus Event
episodes.summary: Loki and Sylvie's growing bond causes a branch in the timeline serious enough to draw the TVA's full attention.

deepDive.plot: A flashback shows Sylvie as a child being taken from Asgard by Renslayer. On Lamentis, waiting to die, Loki and Sylvie sit together and the connection between two variants of the same person who were never supposed to meet creates a nexus event large enough for the TVA to find them. They are pulled out seconds before the moon is destroyed. Mobius starts pulling at the thread and finds Sylvie is right: he retrieves his own file and realises he was a variant too, taken from a life on the timeline. Renslayer prunes him for it. B-15 takes Loki and Sylvie to the Time-Keepers' chamber, where the three rulers of the TVA are revealed to be androids with nobody behind them. Renslayer prunes Loki as well. Rather than dying, he wakes somewhere else, and four other versions of himself are standing over him.

watchFor.name: The Void's Loki variants
watchFor.thisFilm: A group of Loki variants exiled to the end of time is glimpsed, including a child version and an alligator.
watchFor.future: Expands on just how many timeline branches and variants of a single character can exist.

episodes.title: Journey Into Mystery
episodes.summary: Loki meets a collection of his own variants exiled to a wasteland at the end of time, guarded by a terrifying creature.

deepDive.plot: Being pruned does not kill you. It drops you in the Void at the end of time, where everything the TVA deletes piles up and a creature called Alioth eats whatever moves. Loki finds a settlement of surviving Loki variants living under the wreckage: Classic Loki, Kid Loki, Boastful Loki and an alligator. They tell him nobody escapes, and that every one of them ended up here for the same reason, which is trying to be something other than what the story says a Loki is. Back at the TVA, Sylvie makes Renslayer prune her so she can follow him. She works out that Alioth is a guard rather than a scavenger, which means there is something behind it worth guarding. Loki and Sylvie enchant Alioth together, with Classic Loki dying to buy them the distraction, and the storm parts to show a citadel at the end of time.

episodes.title: For All Time. Always.
episodes.summary: Loki and Sylvie reach the being secretly controlling the TVA from behind the curtain, and must decide the fate of the entire multiverse.

deepDive.plot: Loki and Sylvie walk into the citadel and meet He Who Remains, who has been expecting them and has scripted most of what they are about to say. He explains what he is: a thirty-first century scientist who discovered the other timelines, whose variants discovered them at the same time, and whose war against them nearly ended everything. He won, isolated one timeline, and built the TVA to prune the rest. He is old and tired and wants to hand the job over. The offer is straightforward. Take the chair and keep the single timeline, or kill him and let it branch, in which case his variants come back and the war starts again. Loki believes him. Sylvie does not, and she has spent her whole life wanting this one thing. They fight, she pushes Loki back through a time door, and she kills him. The timeline splits into countless branches. Loki gets back to the TVA and finds Mobius and B-15 do not know who he is, and the statues in the atrium are no longer of the Time-Keepers. They are of Kang.

watchFor.name: He Who Remains
watchFor.thisFilm: Reveals himself as the true architect of the TVA, having ended a war between his own variants by pruning every other timeline.
watchFor.future: His death fractures the Sacred Timeline into a true multiverse, and a variant of him becomes a major villain later.

movies.title: Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania
movies.summary: Scott Lang and his family are pulled into the Quantum Realm, where they run headfirst into a powerful being who has been waiting there for a very long time.

beforeWatch.context: Scott Lang helped save the universe in Endgame and has been enjoying it ever since. He has written a book and people stop him in the street. Two things are worth noting. Scott spent the five years of the Blip trapped in the Quantum Realm, which was about five hours from where he was standing, and Cassie was never dusted, so she lived all five of those years without her father. Janet van Dyne spent more than thirty years down there before Hank and Hope got her out at the end of Ant-Man and the Wasp, and she has never talked about any of it. Unrelated, but if you are following narrative order, this is a good point to watch What If...?, the same recommendation made back in Loki. It is not important to the wider MCU, but it runs on the same idea of infinite possibilities.

deepDive.plot: Scott Lang has been coasting on his part in undoing the Snap, writing a memoir and getting recognised in the street, while his daughter Cassie has been getting arrested at protests and building her own tech. Cassie has made a device that maps the Quantum Realm by sending a signal down into it. Janet van Dyne recognises what it is doing and lunges to shut it off, and the signal pulls all five of them in. Down there they find a populated world, and Janet's thirty years finally get explained. She met Kang the Conqueror, a variant exiled to the Realm by his own kind, and helped repair the multiversal core of his ship before she understood what he was. When she found out he had erased whole timelines, she blew the core apart and stranded him. Kang has spent the time since conquering the Quantum Realm and waiting for a way out. He offers Scott a deal, his family's way home in exchange for the core, and Scott shrinks into it to bring it back. Kang takes the core and breaks the deal. Darren Cross, rebuilt by Kang as MODOK, turns on him at the end, and Scott and Hope overload the core to stop him escaping. The mid-credits fills an arena with thousands more Kangs, and the post-credits drops into 1901, where Loki and Mobius are watching a nervous inventor with the same face.
deepDive.significance: Darren Cross is back. The Yellowjacket from the first Ant-Man, last seen shrinking uncontrollably into nothing, has been found in the Quantum Realm and rebuilt by Kang into MODOK, some kind of mechanized organism designed ONLY for killing. The larger introduction is the man who looks almost exactly like He Who Remains from Loki. This is a different variant, Kang the Conqueror, and the film fills in what the citadel only sketched: he was exiled here by his own variants, and what he wants is out, so he can go back to conquering. The mid-credits scene then fills an arena with thousands more of him, the Council of Kangs, which was the setup for an entire saga built around the character. That plan was abandoned after the legal trouble involving Jonathan Majors, who played him. None of that makes the film skippable, because the post-credit scene leads directly into the second season of Loki.
deepDive.orderNote: Sits between the two seasons of Loki. The man in the citadel at the end of Season 1 has to land before this film's villain makes any sense, and this film's post-credit scene runs straight into Season 2.

watchFor.name: Cassie's age
watchFor.thisFilm: Scott lost five years in the Quantum Realm that only cost him five hours. Cassie lived every one of them without him, and the teenager arguing with him here is the result of a gap he never experienced.

watchFor.name: Janet van Dyne's thirty years
watchFor.thisFilm: The film finally answers what she was doing down there, and the answer is that she met Kang, helped him, worked out what he was, and stranded him. She's been not telling anyone since.

watchFor.name: Cassie Lang
watchFor.thisFilm: Built her own shrinking tech, has been arrested for protesting, and is far more willing to be a hero than her father would like.
watchFor.future: The film sets her up as a Young Avenger, one of several the MCU has introduced without ever putting the team together. She has not appeared since.

watchFor.name: Kang the Conqueror
watchFor.thisFilm: Exiled to the Quantum Realm by his own variants and stripped of his ship. He isn't a man who wants to conquer, he's a man who already did it across countless timelines and got outvoted.

watchFor.name: MODOK
watchFor.thisFilm: Darren Cross from the first Ant-Man, rebuilt by Kang into something with a very large head. The film plays him for laughs, which people either loved or hated.

watchFor.name: The Council of Kangs
watchFor.thisFilm: The mid-credits fills an arena with variants of the man Scott just beat, and they're annoyed that he was killed rather than worried about it. It ends up leading nowhere.
watchFor.future: The next two Avengers films were built on this scene before the plan changed. Doomsday is not the film it was setting up.

watchFor.name: Victor Timely (post-credit)
watchFor.thisFilm: The post-credits drops into 1901, where a nervous inventor is demonstrating impossible machines while Loki and Mobius watch from the back of the room.
watchFor.future: It's a direct trailer for Loki season two.

movies.title: Loki: Season 2
movies.summary: With the timeline shattered and the TVA in disarray, Loki is torn loose in time itself and races to hold the fraying agency together before its machinery, and every branching reality it was built to police, comes apart.

beforeWatch.context: This picks up in the moment Season 1 ended. Sylvie killed He Who Remains at the citadel, and with him went the one thing holding the Sacred Timeline to a single thread. The branches have been multiplying ever since, faster and faster, and nothing was built to handle that. Loki was thrown back into a TVA where nobody recognises him and where the statues in the atrium are of another Kang variant rather than the Time-Keepers. Worth having fresh as well is the post-credit scene of Quantumania, with Loki and Mobius watching a nervous inventor put on a show. This season is much more of a workplace ensemble than the first, and considerably more technical.

deepDive.plot: Loki is thrown back into the TVA from the citadel and immediately starts time-slipping, dragged between the organisation's past and future without warning. Mobius and a repair technician called Ouroboros pull him out of it. The problem underneath is the Temporal Loom, the machine that weaves the branching timelines into something stable. It was built for one thread, there are now more branches every second than it can process, and it is going to blow. The Loom was made to Victor Timely's designs, so the TVA go looking for him and find him at the 1893 World's Fair in Chicago, a nervous showman selling impossible machines he built out of a TVA handbook Ravonna Renslayer gave him as a child. Renslayer and Miss Minutes are hunting him too, both still loyal to what He Who Remains built. Timely is brought in and killed by temporal radiation before he can do anything useful. Every engineering fix fails, and when the Loom finally goes it takes the TVA and everyone in it apart. Loki uses his time-slipping to go back, over and over, for centuries, learning temporal mechanics from OB until he can control where he lands. Eventually he works out that the Loom was never the answer, because the machine only exists to keep the branches down to one. So he walks out to the end of time himself, tears the Loom apart, and takes hold of the branches by hand.
deepDive.significance: The conclusion to the TVA story, and it lands somewhere almost nobody predicted. The organisation comes out of it doing the opposite of the job it was built for. It no longer prunes branches, it protects them and lets them grow. Part of that new job is hunting down the Kang variants still out there, and there is a blink-and-you-miss-it moment near the end where the file on the Earth-616 variant is closed, which is the one Scott Lang dealt with in Quantumania. Loki's own ending is the real surprise. A prince of Asgard, rightful king of Jotunheim, burdened with 'glorious purpose', makes a choice that nobody witnesses and nobody ever will, and trades his ambition for eternal isolation, physically holding the fracturing branches of reality together for all eternity. A purpose that's not so glorious.
deepDive.orderNote: Straight after Season 1, which it continues from the same moment. Quantumania sits before it so that Kang's motives have been laid out properly before this season has to deal with the rest of him.

watchFor.name: The Temporal Loom
watchFor.thisFilm: The machine the TVA uses to weave branching timelines into one, failing because it was built for a single thread and there are now far too many. Most of the season is an engineering problem.

watchFor.name: Victor Timely
watchFor.thisFilm: A variant of the man from the citadel, found at the 1893 World's Fair in Chicago building machines out of a TVA handbook Ravonna handed him as a child. He's a nervous showman and a bit of a con artist, nothing like the original, which is the point the season is making about variants. The TVA need him because the Loom was built to his designs, and he is vaporised by temporal radiation the moment he steps out onto the gangway to fix it.

watchFor.name: Miss Minutes
watchFor.thisFilm: The cartoon mascot, which was never a mascot. Her loyalty is to the man who built her, and she's been steering things since before the series started. She is rebooted afterwards, and OB restores her to the new TVA.

watchFor.name: Mobius
watchFor.thisFilm: Learns what his life was before the TVA took it, goes to look at it, and doesn't knock on the door. He resigns once the crisis is over and drives out to watch his sons from across the road.

watchFor.name: Hunter B-15
watchFor.thisFilm: Spends the season arguing that the workforce deserve to know they were all taken from lives of their own, and she's proved right. She's promoted into one of the senior roles at the TVA by the end of it.
watchFor.future: She turns up again at the end of Deadpool & Wolverine.

watchFor.name: Loki's century of failure
watchFor.thisFilm: Once he can steer his own time-slipping, Loki goes back to the same moment again and again for centuries, learning temporal mechanics from OB until he understands the machine better than the people who built it. Every single attempt to save everyone fails. That is what it takes before he stops trying to repair the Loom.

watchFor.name: What Loki chooses
watchFor.thisFilm: He stops trying to fix the Loom and takes its place instead, holding every branch himself, alone, forever. It's the throne he wanted in the first film, redefined into the loneliest job that exists. His existence is now the anchor the whole structure hangs from, and it is the reason every crossover, every incursion and every bit of timeline-hopping after this can happen without the branches collapsing into nothing.

watchFor.name: Yggdrasil
watchFor.thisFilm: The last shot pulls back on the branches Loki is holding, and they've arranged themselves into the shape of a tree. It's Yggdrasil, the World Tree that holds the realms together in Norse myth, which is where Asgard and the rest of it came from in the first place.
watchFor.future: Loki has an important role in the Avengers films still to come.

episodes.title: Ouroboros
episodes.summary: Loki is scattered through time by 'time-slipping' after the season one finale and must be rescued by Mobius and the TVA's repair technician, OB.

deepDive.plot: Loki lands back in the TVA from the citadel and is immediately yanked forward into a version of it that has been wrecked, where a Mobius who does not know him has him arrested. He slips back and forth between the two without any control over it. Present-day Mobius and Hunter B-15 get hold of him, and Loki tries to explain that the man behind the whole organisation is dead and that the Time-Keepers were a lie. They take him down to Repairs and Advancement, where they meet Ouroboros, the technician who has been working alone down there for four hundred years and who wrote the handbook everyone else ignores. OB rigs a temporal aura extractor to pull Loki out of the slipping, which needs someone at the Temporal Loom to pull a switch at the exact moment. It works, barely. What it also reveals is the real problem: the Loom is straining, the branches are multiplying faster than it can weave them, and it is heading for a meltdown that takes everything with it.

episodes.title: Breaking Brad
episodes.summary: Loki and the team track down a rogue variant impersonating a TV star while the TVA's timeline monitors start to fail.

deepDive.plot: Loki and Mobius go after Hunter X-5, one of the agents sent to find Sylvie, who has abandoned the job and is living in 1977 London as a film star called Brad Wolfe. They bring him in, and getting Sylvie's location out of him takes Mobius doing something he is not proud of in an interrogation room. Meanwhile General Dox has taken a faction of hunters and gone rogue, bombing branched timelines out of existence rather than letting them run, which is the old doctrine taken to its end point. Loki and Mobius reach Sylvie in 1982 Oklahoma, where she is working in a McDonald's and has no interest in any of it. The episode ends with Sylvie finding Dox and her unit, and killing them.

episodes.summary: The hunt for a new variant leads Loki and Mobius to a World's Fair in 19th-century Chicago.

deepDive.plot: A flashback shows Renslayer and Miss Minutes handing a TVA handbook to a small boy in 1868 Chicago, telling him he will do great things. That boy grew into Victor Timely, and by the 1893 World's Fair he is a showman with a stutter and a nervous line in patter, selling machines built from a book he never fully understood. Loki, Mobius and Sylvie try to reach him before Renslayer does. Sylvie's instinct is to kill him on sight, because he wears the face of the man she already killed once, and Loki has to talk her down. There is a chase through the fair over the handbook, Renslayer and Miss Minutes get their hands on Timely briefly, and Renslayer's own history with He Who Remains comes out in the middle of it. Timely gets away on a train with the book, and the TVA leave with nothing except the knowledge that the man who designed the Loom is alive and findable.

episodes.title: Heart of the TVA
episodes.summary: With the timeline branching out of control, the team races to stabilize the Temporal Loom before it destroys everything.

deepDive.plot: Timely is brought into the TVA and put to work with OB on a throughput multiplier, a way of widening the Loom so it can handle the branches instead of being overwhelmed by them. Renslayer arrives and makes her case for being given the organisation back, and Sylvie prunes her, sending her to the Void. Timely is the only one who can install the multiplier, which means walking out onto the gangway into the radiation. He goes. He is vaporised before he reaches the end of it, and the multiplier is never fitted. The Loom goes critical. Everyone still standing in the TVA comes apart as the whole place spaghettifies, and Loki is left slipping through time on his own.

episodes.title: Science/Fiction
episodes.summary: Loki goes looking for the people he worked with, and finds them living lives that have nothing to do with him.

deepDive.plot: With the TVA gone, Loki slips down onto the timeline and finds everyone scattered back into the lives they were taken from. Mobius is Don, selling jet skis in Ohio with two sons. OB is a science fiction writer with a book nobody bought. Casey is a criminal. B-15 is a doctor. Sylvie is back in 1982 Oklahoma. None of them know him, and he has to talk each of them into remembering something they never lived through. He gets them together and they nearly work the problem out, and then the branch they are standing on starts to disintegrate too, because without the Loom there is nothing holding any of it. What Loki takes from it is the one thing that matters: he can steer the slipping now. He does not have to be dragged. He can choose when to land.

watchFor.name: Sylvie's other life
watchFor.thisFilm: The McDonald's in 1982 Oklahoma is the closest thing to a life she has ever had, and she says plainly that she would rather have it than a purpose. She is the only one who does not want to be talked out of the life she is living.

episodes.title: Glorious Purpose
episodes.summary: Loki keeps going back to the same moment, looking for the one version of it where everybody makes it out.

deepDive.plot: Loki spends centuries in the same handful of minutes. He slips back to before the Loom failed, over and over, learning temporal mechanics from OB one lesson at a time until he understands the machine better than the man who designed it. Every attempt fails. He tries fixing the Loom, he tries getting Timely to the gangway faster, he tries going back further and stopping Sylvie at the citadel, and none of it holds, because the Loom was only ever built to keep the branches down to one and there are far too many now. He goes to see He Who Remains, who tells him the only options are his way or nothing. He goes to see Sylvie, who tells him to work out what he actually wants rather than what he is afraid of. So Loki walks up the stairs to the end of time on his own, tears the Loom apart, and catches the dying branches in his hands. He carries them to the throne and sits down, and the timelines run out from him into the shape of a tree. Afterwards, the TVA carries on with the opposite job: protecting the branches instead of pruning them, and going after the Kang variants still out there. Mobius resigns and goes to look at the family he never had. B-15 is running things.

watchFor.name: Loki as the multiverse's anchor
watchFor.thisFilm: Chooses to wind himself around every timeline, permanently sacrificing his own future to keep the multiverse from collapsing.

movies.title: Deadpool & Wolverine
movies.summary: Recruited by the TVA to help save his own universe from being erased, a reluctant Deadpool drags a jaded variant of Wolverine along on a chaotic, foul-mouthed multiversal detour.

beforeWatch.context: Because Disney bought Fox, this is the first Deadpool film that is officially part of the MCU. The two before it were made by Fox and are not, and they are set in a separate reality entirely, Earth-10005, which is where Wade is from. At the end of Deadpool 2 he steals Cable's time-travel device to stop Vanessa being killed, then keeps going and undoes a run of other things he did not like, putting branches through his own timeline as he goes. Logan is set in that same universe. In it, Charles Xavier has an uncontrolled seizure that kills the X-Men, Logan spends what is left of his life keeping him hidden, and he dies trying to save Laura, the girl grown from his own genes. That Logan has lived through every one of the earlier X-Men films. The other thing to carry in is the TVA, who after the second season of Loki are still there and still managing the timelines. One note on the order below: Logan is listed before Deadpool 2, because Deadpool 2 spoils the ending of Logan when Wade breaks the fourth wall about it, even though Deadpool 2 happens more than ten years earlier. If you don't mind the spoiler, swap them back.

optionalViewing: X-Men: Days of Future Past (2014, timeline reset)

deepDive.plot: Wade Wilson gave up being Deadpool after failing his Avengers audition, and he sells used cars now. He does still have Cable's time-travel device, and the film opens with him using it to go forward to 2029 and dig up Logan's grave, nearly a decade ahead of his own present. TVA agents are waiting for him there. An executive called Paradox tells him his universe is dying, because its anchor being was Wolverine and Wolverine is dead. Paradox offers to move Wade to a surviving timeline and let the rest of Earth-10005 go. Wade would rather save everyone he knows, so he steals a TemPad and goes looking for a replacement, working through Logan variant after Logan variant until he finds one who was too late to save his own X-Men and has been drinking about it ever since. Paradox prunes them both to the Void, the dumping ground at the end of time where everything the TVA deletes ends up, still patrolled by Alioth. The Void is run by Cassandra Nova, Charles Xavier's twin sister, who was never let out into the world. Wade and Logan fall in with a resistance made up of other discarded characters, Elektra, Blade, Gambit and Laura among them, and the deal they cut with Nova goes wrong. Paradox has built a machine that can unmake a timeline from the outside, Nova takes it off him, and she starts with Wade's. Wade and Logan grab hold of it together, which should kill either of them alone, and between the two of them they survive it. Nova is finished, the TVA arrive to arrest Paradox, and Earth-10005 holds. Logan has nothing to go back to, so he goes home with Wade, to a point in that timeline where everyone Wade knows is still alive.
deepDive.significance: The first MCU film released with an R rating. It is less a film that moves the larger plot along and more a send-off for the Fox era, made because Disney bought the studio that owned all of it. Wesley Snipes plays Blade again, Chris Evans turns up as Johnny Storm rather than as Steve Rogers, and Channing Tatum finally gets to play the Gambit he was cast as years before that film was cancelled. It also introduces the idea of an anchor being, one person so central to a universe that the whole thing comes apart without them. At the end Wade brings Logan home to Earth-10005 to live among his friends. That is the same universe Fox's X-Men belong to, and the point Wade returns to sits nearly a decade before 2029, so all of them are still alive.
deepDive.orderNote: Set outside time, and placed after both seasons of Loki, because the TVA is what starts the plot and this is the version of the organisation that comes out of the second season.

watchFor.name: TVA
watchFor.thisFilm: Still pruning, still convinced it knows best. The one Wade has to deal with is Paradox, a senior figure inside the organisation rather than the man in charge of it, who would rather hurry a dying universe along than wait for it to run out on its own.
watchFor.future: The organisation has an important part to play in Avengers: Doomsday.

watchFor.name: Anchor beings
watchFor.thisFilm: The film's rule is that some universes are held together by one person, and when that person dies the universe unravels. Wade's anchor was his Logan, and his Logan is dead when the film opens.

watchFor.name: Logan
watchFor.thisFilm: Not the Logan from the Fox films' ending. A variant who was too late to save his X-Men and has been drinking about it since, wearing the yellow suit for the first time on screen.
